LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Here's how to watch, what to know, and an expert prediction before the Pats and Bears face off in Chicago Getty Images In the Week 7 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Chicago Bears play host to the New England Patriots . Chicago is coming off a win in Caleb Williams ' return to the lineup, having held on for a 31-23 victory in a game that moved the Bears to 4-2 on the season. The Bears bounced back from their dispiriting loss to the division rival Green Bay Packers the week before, when the offense looked like a disaster with backup Tyson Bagent under center. Chicago will look to keep the good times rolling here. New England also won what -- on the surface -- looked like a close game against the New York Jets , but finished with a seven-point margin of victory thanks only to a late field goal. The Patriots have won three consecutive games after starting the season 1-2, and their quarterback has found a groove after looking nearly broken to start the year. The Pats, too, are looking to keep the train on the tracks on Thursday night. Will the Bears capture another win, or will the Patriots continue their hot streak? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Bears vs. Patriots live Date: Thursday, Oct. 22 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Soldier Field (Chicago) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bears -3, O/U 50.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Patriots have the ball Drake Maye has found himself over the last three weeks, completing 66 of 103 passes for 878 yards, 10 touchdowns, and one interception after going just 51-of-80 for 585 yards, one touchdown, and six picks through the first three games of the season. Maye has rediscovered the deep ball, in particular, going 12 of 20 for 350 yards and four scores on throws beyond 15 yards in the last three games, per Tru Media. Before that, he was just 9 of 20 for 281 yards and four interceptions on those throws. Maye finished with a strong game against the Jets despite A.J. Brown looking horrifyingly bad in his return from an ankle injury. Brown dropped (at least) three passes and turned his 10 targets into only 27 yards. Maye also lost Romeo Doubs to a shoulder injury on an early-game touchdown pass, so he was working with a limited receiving corps behind Brown. Still, he threw for 235 yards and three touchdowns without turning the ball over. Brown will presumably be better here, and Chicago hasn't been great against outside receivers, but last week's return of Kyler Gordon could lead to slot man Demario Douglas having a tougher go of things than he has over the last few weeks. Kyle Williams could get in on the action with Doubs sidelined, though Efton Chism has been getting more snaps because the Patriots trust him as a blocker. Chicago checks in a surprising eighth in opponents' EPA per dropback so far this season, per Tru Media, thanks to a high sack rate and a few timely interceptions. Opponents have averaged 8.4 yards per attempt against the Bears, though, indicating that you can indeed move the ball through the air if you can get a pass off and avoid a turnover. Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen has generated pressure at an above-average rate (39.7% of dropbacks) despite working with a somewhat limited group up front, and the Patriots will be without two starting guards here. So, the running backs (particularly Rhamondre Stevenson ) will have to be on their game in pass protection on Thursday night. The Patriots have struggled to run the ball thus far this season, with Stevenson, TreVeyon Henderson and Corey Kiner combining for an average of just 3.9 yards per carry on 151 rushing attempts. Stevenson leads the way in the backfield largely because the Patriots trust him the most in short yardage and pass protection, but he hasn't been efficient or explosive. Henderson had an explosive rushing touchdown on his first run of the season but has failed to record one since. Kiner was a little-used third-stringer until he salted away the game against the Jets last Sunday. He could perhaps work his way into more touches after a nice showing in that game, given the rushing struggles of the two leads and the fact that Henderson also fumbled against New York. The Bears have allowed opponents 4.4 yards per carry on running-back rushes so far this season, with much of the success coming by way of yards before contact. It may be difficult for the Patriots to generate those types of yards with their injury issues along the offensive line, and their backs haven't exactly done the best job of breaking tackles this year, so the challenge of moving the offense down the field will likely fall squarely on Maye's right shoulder. When the Bears have the ball Caleb Williams returned last week from a three-game absence due to a hamstring injury and looked no worse for wear. Williams completed 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards and a touchdown. The Bears kept things simple for him with a 3.9-yard average depth of throw (eighth-lowest for any quarterback in a single game this season), per Tru Media, and he was extremely efficient as a result. Williams has only played in three games so far this year, but he's leading the league with a 72.5% completion rate and is up to a career-best 7.8 yards per attempt. And that's despite a truly awful game against the Vikings in Week 2, where he went 15-of-26 for just 138 yards and an interception. In his first couple of appearances, it seemed like journeyman wideout Kalif Raymond (14 targets in Weeks 1 and 2) was his primary option, but on Sunday, it was Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland -- the most expected options -- leading the way with eight and seven targets, respectively. Rome Odunze saw five looks. Given the way they're each deployed, it seems likely that Odunze will see a bunch of Christian Gonzalez 's coverage on Thursday night -- especially with Carlton Davis III ruled out. Odunze is the biggest of the trio and plays most often on the perimeter, and he also tends to run the most routes. If that's the way things go, we should expect the passing game to flow through Burden and Loveland yet again. The Patriots have allowed opponents to complete 31 of 46 passes for 301 yards on throws to the slot this season, per Tru Media. Burden could have a nice night working inside if he's on the field more often than he was last week (eight targets on only 18 routes), though Marcus Jones does have an interception this season and is allowing only 1.46 yards per coverage snap in the slot, per Pro Football Focus. By contrast, New England has allowed only 29 catches for 279 yards to tight ends to date, so Loveland may not find the coverage as friendly. The Bears would do well to line him up all over the formation rather than solely in line, and perhaps use multi-tight end sets where he plays more of a receiver role, and Cole Kmet or Sam Roush handles the blocking aspects of the position. The Bears also tried against Atlanta to do what they do best: run the ball with volume. D'Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson (the latter filling in for the injured Kyle Monangai ) combined for 29 carries. They ran for only 96 yards on those totes, but they did find the end zone three times. Chicago's offensive line actually created some nice push, generating 1.45 yards before contact per carry, according to Tru Media, but the backs slumped to only 1.83 yards after contact, as they combined for only four broken tackles. (For context, consider that the Seahawks ' running backs combined for 10 in their awful game against the Broncos on Thursday night.) The Pats have allowed only 3.9 yards per rush this season, thanks in part to yielding an average of only 0.75 yards before contact. Swift and Johnson (Monangai is out again) will have to do a better job of breaking tackles this time around if they want to generate yardage and create favorable down-and-distance scenarios for Williams and the passing game. I see this being a high-scoring game, what with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images What did we learn in Week 6? The Houston Texans are officially back, as is Caleb Williams with the Chicago Bears , and we have some serious questions about the Los Angeles Rams , who were upset by the Arizona Cardinals at home last Sunday. The Cardinals now have more wins at SoFi Stadium this year than the Rams and Los Angeles Chargers combined. This week, the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints will play the first-ever NFL game in Paris, the San Francisco 49ers look to remain perfect against the Atlanta Falcons , and Kenneth Walker III aims to lead the Kansas City Chiefs to victory over his former team, the Seattle Seahawks . This could be a revenge game for the ages. Which teams should you pick in Week 7, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 21 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. New England Patriots at Chicago Bears (-3) (TNF) Dajani (Bears -3): I can't remember the last time I've been this excited for a Thursday night game. Caleb Williams will suit up for the first time at home since his hamstring injury, and this is the first Bears home game since the passing of Mike Ditka. I have concerns about this Bears pass defense and how it will fare against a red-hot Drake Maye , but the fact is that Chicago has allowed 9.3 points per game at home this season. The Bears' offense has also averaged 35 points per game in their four wins, and I think Williams is out to make a statement. This will be a high-flying affair that comes down to the very end, and a push is very much in play. But give me Chicago at home, with the backing of an emotionally charged atmosphere. Remember, the Bears' lone Super Bowl win came against the New England Patriots under Ditka. … Prediction: Bears 28, Patriots 24 Dubin (Bears -3): I also see this being a high-scoring game, with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. … Prediction: Bears 31, Patriots 27 Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) vs. New Orleans Saints (Paris) Dajani (Saints +3.5): The Steelers are impossible to figure out. From week-to-week — or even half-to-half, as evidenced by last week's overtime victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . If you're going to give me the hook at +3.5 in an international game, I'm probably going to take it. The Saints are a perfect 8-0 ATS in their last eight games away from home, and are 3-0 ATS all-time in international games. I think Gayle Benson's recent comments stirred up the locker room, and the Saints responded with a win in which they dropped 34 points — even if it came against the New York Giants . … Prediction: Steelers 23, Saints 20 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): The Saints finally played a game from ahead last week against the Giants, and they didn't necessarily look comfortable doing it. They have mostly been a second-half offensive team throughout this season, struggling early on before piling up yards and points in comeback mode. The New England Patriots and Drake Maye are riding a three-game winning streak into their primetime matchup with the Chicago Bears and former No. 1 overall pick Caleb Williams on Thursday Night Football. Williams is making his second straight start after he missed three games earlier this season with a hamstring injury. The star quarterback showed no signs of rust in Week 6, completing 30 of his 36 pass attempts in a win over the Atlanta Falcons, improving the Bears to 4-2 this season. Chicago is favored in this matchup, and it needs every win it can get with the NFC North sporting four teams over .500 through the first six weeks. The Bears may be getting a little extra love in this matchup because of all the injuries for the Patriots, who have been decimated at receiver (Mack Hollins and Romeo Doubs on IR) and on their offensive line. Still, New England has won three games in a row, and Maye is back in the MVP conversation with 10 touchdown passes during that streak. He has a tough matchup ahead against a Chicago team that is in the top 10 in the league in EPA/Play and success rate on defense this season. So, how should bettors attack Thursday’s showdown? In the leadup to this marquee matchup, the SI Betting team has made a bunch of game picks, prop bet selections and more. I’ve decided to share some of our favorites all in one place to help bettors get the most of this primetime matchup between two playoff contenders in Week 7. Best NFL Picks and Predictions for Patriots vs. Bears Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook New England Patriots vs. Chicago Bears UNDER 50.5 (-105) – Iain MacMillan Drake Maye OVER 1.5 Passing Touchdowns (-116) – Peter Dewey Colston Loveland Anytime TD (+170) – Peter Dewey D’Andre Swift UNDER 61.5 Rushing Yards (-115) – Peter Dewey This week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan shared his favorite bet for this matchup in his Road to 272 column , where he picks every game of the NFL season. He’s taking the UNDER even with two star quarterbacks facing off: Unless I'm missing something, I'm not quite sure why the total for this game is in the 50s. Sure, the Bears' offense is much more explosive with Caleb Williams at quarterback, but even with that being the case, these two offenses rank 12th and 14th in EPA per play this season and seventh and 12th in success rate. A high total would make sense if the two defenses in this game were bad, but they rank in the top half of the league in most metrics. In fact, the Bears' defense comes into this game ranking fourth in opponent success rate. The Patriots' offense is also dealing with some injuries. A.J. Brown is questionable, and Romeo Doubs is on IR. Their run game can't be relied on to help out the injuries at wide receiver, as it's been largely ineffective all season. I'll bet the UNDER on Thursday Night Football for the second straight week. Maye started the season in an awful slump, throwing just one score and six picks in his first three games. Since then, he’s flipped the script, tossing 10 scores (at least three in each game) over the last three weeks, leading New England to wins over Buffalo, Las Vegas and the New York Jets. Maye is right back in the mix to win the MVP, and I like this matchup against a Chicago defense that has allowed nine passing scores in 2026 and was torched by Bryce Young and Jordan Love already this season. The Bears have benefitted from some soft scheduling in terms of the quarterbacks they’ve faced, but Love threw for 367 yards against them in Week 5, and Chicago has allowed the 15th-most passing yards in the league. New England loves to throw the ball, and I think the odds for this prop are pretty favorable considering the fact that Maye threw 31 touchdown passes in 2025. Bears tight end Colston Loveland had a breakout showing in Week 6, catching six of his seven targets for 65 yards and a score. Williams only threw one touchdown in Week 6, but Loveland was targeted multiple times in the end zone – Caleb just missed him for a second score. Last season, the young tight end really came on in the second half, finishing the campaign with six touchdown receptions. He’s only picked up one in 2026, and New England has allowed just one receiving score to the position this season. Still, Loveland’s role is growing with 21 targets over the last three games. He’s a solid bet at this price after his best game of the season. D’Andre Swift has a ton of carries for the Bears this season, handling 94 touches for 398 yards and six scores on the ground, but he hasn’t been super efficient since Week 1. Swift ran for 124 yards on 18 carries against Carolina in the season opener, yet he has just one other game (Week 3 against Philadelphia) where he’s picked up over 60 rushing yards. Backup Kyle Monangai (turf toe) has been banged up, but Swift still split time with Roschon Johnson in Week 6 and has played just 56.7 percent of the Bears’ snaps this season. New England is allowing just 3.9 yards per carry in the 2026 campaign, and I wouldn’t be shocked if Swift came up short of this rushing total again on Thursday. He has averaged less than four yards per carry in two of the last three weeks, putting up 58, 43 and 44 rushing yards during that stretch. Even if the volume is there for the veteran back, I think he’s a fade candidate in Week 7. Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. home.headline: Report: Bears TE Cole Kmet (knee) likely out for season
home.blurb: Drafted by Chicago in the second round out of Notre Dame in 2020, Kmet has collected 298 catches for 3,026 yards and 22 TDs in 107 career games (94 starts). Kmet was carted off the field in the fourth quarter of Thursday night's 30-24 home victory against the New England Patriots. He grabbed his right knee after being tackled low following an 8-yard catch and finished with three receptions for 28 yards. "He's a big part of our heartbeat," Johnson said. "It stinks. I hate it." Kmet, 27, had 10 receptions for 87 yards and one touchdown in seven games (three starts) this season. He has one season left on a four-year, $50 million contract extension signed in July 2023. Johnson said Kmet's absence is an opportunity for 2026 third-round pick Sam Roush to step up. Roush, 23, has three catches for 33 yards in seven games this season for the Bears (5-2). "We'll be able to see the player that we drafted," Johnson said. "We had high hopes when we took him. ... I'm confident in what he's going to be able to do for us back half of the season." home.headline: What we learned about Caleb Williams and Chicago Bears in NFL Week 6
home.source: USA TODAY College Sports Wire on MSN
home.blurb: The Chicago Bears were ignited by the return of former USC Trojan Caleb Williams and teammate Kyler Gordon. Both players did not miss a beat and put together dominant performances. As a result, the Bears ' offense and defense both looked good enough to make a run at the Super Bowl. Coltson Loveland was disappointing at the start of the season. Last week, however, the return of starting quarterback Caleb Williams helped him get his confidence back. Loveland had a spectacular touchdown catch on the opening drive, and he finished with 6 catches for 65 yards. The Bears offense is at its best when Loveland is making plays. It looks like the Bears' biggest playmaker is back. The NFC conference is wide open and up for grabs. The San Francisco 49ers and the Minnesota Vikings are both undefeated, but both teams have weaknesses the Bears can exploit. When this Bears team is healthy and with the return of Kyle Monangai on offense, the Bears can beat anyone in the league. Here is what we learned about the Bears in NFL Week 6: Caleb Williams looks like a top 5 quarterback One of the biggest weaknesses of Caleb Williams' game is his accuracy and his ability to play on time. Against the Atlanta Falcons, those weaknesses looked like strengths. Caleb started the game off 24/24, not missing a beat. He finished the game with an 83.3% completion percentage. That proves Caleb Williams is one of the best quarterbacks in the league. Right now, he leads the NFL with a 72.5% completion percentage. His development in year 3 has been exciting to watch and scary for the rest of the NFL to see. Kyle Monangai is such a pivotal piece to the offense Without Kyle Monangai, the Bears' run game has taken a big hit. He is the physical back that this offense needs. Without him, D'Andre Swift is a lot easier to limit. In his last game, Monangai had 30 carries for 146 yards and a touchdown. Through just 4 games, he has 324 yards and 3 touchdowns. In his absence, his true value to the offense has been on full display. It was too early to close the door on Colston Loveland When healthy Kyler Gordon is one of the best at his position in the NFL In only 16 snaps, Kyler Gordon showed he can make a massive impact. He tallied 3 sacks and a tackle for a loss on his first snap of the season. Dennis Allen is able to get extremely creative when Kyler Gordon is on the field. Gordon could be the key to the Bears' defense going from good to great. home.headline: Chicago Bears confirm suspicions about Cole Kmet's injury, leaving a massive void in the offense and big shoes for a struggling rookie to fill
home.blurb: Kmet immediately had a non-contact issue with his knee prior to contact on the play, and it didn't look good as soon as he went down. As the cart took him off the field, Kmet gave a thumbs-up to the crowd. And shout out to Patriots safety Kevin Byard, the former Bears All-Pro, was there to support Kmet when the cart came out. That speaks volumes about the respect Kmet has earned. But, the initial suspicions that have circulated all morning on Friday have unfortunately been confirmed. Kmet has suffered a serious knee injury and will be placed on the injured reserve, the team confirmed, leaving a massive void in Chicago's offense going into the rest of the season. With Kmet now out, Roush is basically a starter in this offense. Which means he needs to clean up those mistakes and be ready to go right away. The Bears can't afford to let this be a weak link in an offense that leans so heavily on tight ends. Entering Week 7, the Bears had 93 rushing attempts with 2-TEs (most in the NFL), 60 rushing attempts with 3-TEs (4th in the NFL), 87 dropbacks with 2-TEs (2nd in the NFL), and 34 dropbacks with 3-TEs (3rd in the NFL). It's a HUGE part of this offense. The good news is that Roush has already been playing 22 percent of the offensive snaps. So, it's not like the Bears are trotting out a green rookie that hasn't played at all. Still, there's a big difference between rotating in behind veterans and carrying a starter's workload every week. Meanwhile, the Bears could also look to the practice squad for added depth. Tight end Stephen Carlson may be an option Chicago calls up more often in the coming weeks. UDFA rookie Hayden Large is another option the team liked in camp but he's still on the IR. Perhaps the Bears even lean into using Trapilo/Benedet at swing tackle as a jumbo-TE. But given how complex this position is in Johnson's offense, I don't expect the Bears to make outside moves to find a replacement for Kmet. This is where Johnson has to prove the selection of Roush was worth it. Against Tampa Bay he went 4-for-5, with makes from 52 and 58 yards. That was his second straight game with multiple field goals. away.headline: Steelers' TJ Watt pops up on injury report with new concern
away.blurb: The former Defensive Player of the Year didn’t practice on Wednesday for a rest designation. But, then he was limited in practice on Thursday because of a calf injury. This is a new injury to the public. There was some good defensive news coming out of the Steelers’ injury report, though. Cornerback Jalen Ramsey was limited on Thursday after not practicing the day prior with a wrist injury, so that was improvement. Outside linebacker Alex Highsmith was also limited with a groin issue, the same designation as Wednesday. Related Articles Giants DC Threatens Players Amid 'Unacceptable' Behavior, Calls Out 'Traitors' The Pittsburgh Steelers haven’t been able to catch a break from injuries the last few weeks. It seems like a new star player is being added to the injury report each week. Thursday’s injury report included a surprising name, one that Steelers fans wish wasn’t on the list: edge rusher T.J. Watt. It’s unclear when or how Watt suffered the calf injury. But, now there’s a possibility, even if just a slight one, that Watt could miss Sunday’s game in Paris against the New Orleans Saints . Watt being absent for a game is always a loss for the Steelers. He can always make big and important plays for his team. Through six games this season, Watt’s recorded 4.5 sacks (tied for eighth in the league), 15 tackles, one interception, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery. Veteran tackle Cameron Heyward didn’t practice Wednesday or Thursday for rest designations, but he should be good to go come Sunday. Safety DeShon Elliott recorded his second-straight full practice on Thursday, meaning he’ll likely play on Sunday. It would mark Elliott’s first game since last October after he suffered an MCL sprain, hyperextended knee and a hamstring injury. Philadelphia Eagles star quarterback Jalen Hurts is expected to be done for the season after being diagnosed with blood clots in both his lungs and deep vein thrombosis. Now, with Hurts done for the year, the Eagles are being linked to a trade for a Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback. In a recent article for Bleacher Report , Kristopher Knox named the Eagles as a potential suitor for Steelers quarterback Mason Rudolph. "Mason Rudolph remains the most logical trade target for teams seeking a backup quarterback or spot starter midseason. He's one of three reserve QBs that the Pittsburgh Steelers have behind Aaron Rodgers, along with Will Howard and rookie Drew Allar," Knox wrote. "Potential Suitors : Miami Dolphins, Philadelphia Eagles." Rudolph is currently in his seventh NFL season and sixth with the Steelers. In 36 career NFL games split between the Steelers and Tennessee Titans, he has thrown 30 touchdowns, 22 interceptions, 4,925 passing yards, and has completed 64.3% of his passes. He has primarily been a backup quarterback during his career and could be a solid player for the Eagles to add to their group ahead of the deadline.

away.blurb: Saints Final Injury Report: Ruiz, Shepherd questionable for Steelers game in Paris – Crescent City Sports menu The New Orleans Saints will take a healthier roster into Sunday’s international matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers, but questions remain about two key veterans as the teams prepare for their Week 7 showdown at Stade de France. Right guard Cesar Ruiz and defensive lineman Nathan Shepherd were listed as questionable on the Saints’ final injury report Friday. Both players are dealing with issues that could affect New Orleans on both sides of the line of scrimmage in its meeting with Pittsburgh. Ruiz, who sustained a knee injury during last Sunday’s 34-27 victory over the New York Giants, returned to practice Friday on a limited basis after missing the first two sessions of the week. His status will be worth watching, with rookie Jeremiah Wright a potential replacement if Ruiz cannot play. Shepherd was a late-week concern after missing Friday’s practice with an illness. He had participated fully Wednesday and Thursday but remains questionable. Shepherd has missed the Saints’ last two games while dealing with the illness. The Saints received encouraging news at linebacker, where Kaden Elliss and Anfernee Jennings both practiced fully Friday. Elliss has been working his way back from a calf injury, while Jennings has been dealing with a knee injury. Both are expected to be available against Pittsburgh. Kicker Daniel Carlson also returned to practice after missing the first two sessions for personal reasons. As he and his wife are still expecting the birth of their fourth child, Carlson traveled to France to rejoin the team and was a full participant Friday. With potentially challenging weather conditions including the chance for some rain and cross winds expected for the game, New Orleans will be glad to have the veteran specialist in tow Sunday. Running back Alvin Kamara remained limited with a back injury but was not assigned a game-status designation. Quarterback Tyler Shough, who has been managing a left-hand injury, practiced fully throughout the week. Other Saints listed as full participants Friday included running back C.J. Donaldson, cornerback Kool-Aid McKinstry, quarterback Spencer Rattler, defensive lineman Davon Godchaux and offensive lineman Asim Richards, who was added to the report with a hand injury. Pittsburgh will be without wide receiver Ben Skowronek and cornerback Brandin Echols, both ruled out after missing practice throughout the week with calf and hamstring injuries, respectively. Running back Rico Dowdle and safety DeShon Elliott were listed as questionable. Dowdle was limited throughout the week with a knee injury after returning to action last Sunday, while Elliott participated fully in the first two sessions and was listed as a full participant for Friday’s estimated report. home.headline: Saints Final Injury Report: Ruiz, Shepherd questionable for Steelers game in Paris
home.blurb: Saints Final Injury Report: Ruiz, Shepherd questionable for Steelers game in Paris – Crescent City Sports menu The New Orleans Saints will take a healthier roster into Sunday’s international matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers, but questions remain about two key veterans as the teams prepare for their Week 7 showdown at Stade de France. Right guard Cesar Ruiz and defensive lineman Nathan Shepherd were listed as questionable on the Saints’ final injury report Friday. Both players are dealing with issues that could affect New Orleans on both sides of the line of scrimmage in its meeting with Pittsburgh. Ruiz, who sustained a knee injury during last Sunday’s 34-27 victory over the New York Giants, returned to practice Friday on a limited basis after missing the first two sessions of the week. His status will be worth watching, with rookie Jeremiah Wright a potential replacement if Ruiz cannot play. Shepherd was a late-week concern after missing Friday’s practice with an illness. He had participated fully Wednesday and Thursday but remains questionable. Shepherd has missed the Saints’ last two games while dealing with the illness. The Saints received encouraging news at linebacker, where Kaden Elliss and Anfernee Jennings both practiced fully Friday. Elliss has been working his way back from a calf injury, while Jennings has been dealing with a knee injury. Both are expected to be available against Pittsburgh. Kicker Daniel Carlson also returned to practice after missing the first two sessions for personal reasons. As he and his wife are still expecting the birth of their fourth child, Carlson traveled to France to rejoin the team and was a full participant Friday. With potentially challenging weather conditions including the chance for some rain and cross winds expected for the game, New Orleans will be glad to have the veteran specialist in tow Sunday. Running back Alvin Kamara remained limited with a back injury but was not assigned a game-status designation. Quarterback Tyler Shough, who has been managing a left-hand injury, practiced fully throughout the week. Other Saints listed as full participants Friday included running back C.J. Donaldson, cornerback Kool-Aid McKinstry, quarterback Spencer Rattler, defensive lineman Davon Godchaux and offensive lineman Asim Richards, who was added to the report with a hand injury. Pittsburgh will be without wide receiver Ben Skowronek and cornerback Brandin Echols, both ruled out after missing practice throughout the week with calf and hamstring injuries, respectively. Running back Rico Dowdle and safety DeShon Elliott were listed as questionable. Dowdle was limited throughout the week with a knee injury after returning to action last Sunday, while Elliott participated fully in the first two sessions and was listed as a full participant for Friday’s estimated report. home.headline: Saints Injury Report: Cesar Ruiz out again Thursday ahead of Steelers game
home.blurb: Saints Injury Report: Cesar Ruiz out again Thursday ahead of Steelers game – Crescent City Sports menu The New Orleans Saints continued preparations for Sunday's matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Paris on Thursday, with starting right guard Cesar Ruiz remaining sidelined by a knee injury and kicker Daniel Carlson still absent for personal reasons. Ruiz, who sustained the injury during Sunday's 34-27 victory over the New York Giants, did not participate in Thursday's practice after also missing Wednesday's session. His availability is a significant concern for a Saints offensive line preparing to face Pittsburgh's defensive front in Paris. Carlson also missed another practice after not traveling with the Saints to France. Instead, he awaits the arrival of his newborn child. Head coach Kellen Moore previously indicated that the kicker was expected to join the team before Sunday's game. Practice squad kicker Charlie Smyth remains a potential option if Carlson cannot return in time. The Saints added defensive tackle Davon Godchaux to Thursday's report as a non-injury-related rest designation. He did not practice. There was encouraging news elsewhere on the injury report. Quarterback Tyler Shough continued to participate fully despite dealing with a left-hand injury. Backup quarterback Spencer Rattler, who was added to the report with a knee injury Thursday, also practiced fully. Running back C.J. Donaldson was upgraded to full participation after being limited Wednesday with a shoulder injury. Cornerback Kool-Aid McKinstry (head) and defensive tackle Nathan Shepherd (illness) also practiced fully. Linebackers Anfernee Jennings (knee) and Kaden Elliss (calf) remained limited, as did running back Alvin Kamara, who is managing a back injury. Elliss' potential return would be particularly important as the linebacker has missed the previous three games while dealing with the calf injury. He has expressed optimism about playing against Pittsburgh. More clarity should come on Friday with the final injury report. The Week 7 game is apoears to be pivotal. Entering the bye week 3-4 and on a win streak versus 2-5 may the difference for New Orleans between making a push in the NFC South or a disappointing campaign. The Saints face the Steelers on Sunday at Stade de France, with kickoff scheduled for 8:30 a.m. Central time in part of the NFL's international series. picks.blurb: Recently Cut Atlanta Falcons 3rd-Round Pick Puts Raheem Morris, 49ers on Alert Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI Former Atlanta Falcons edge rusher Bralen Trice is exploring his next opportunity after visiting the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday, less than a week after appearing on Atlanta's active roster. The 49ers hosted Trice for a visit after the Falcons released him on Tuesday, Oct. 20. The former third-round pick is looking for a new home after finally making his NFL regular-season debut in 2026, following two injury-plagued seasons in Atlanta. San Francisco's defensive staff includes former Falcons head coach Raheem Morris, now the 49ers' defensive coordinator. Although Morris coached Atlanta in 2024 and 2025, Trice never played under him in a regular-season game. Trice spent his first two NFL seasons sidelined by injuries while Morris led the Falcons. If Trice joins the 49ers, he would be the second former Falcon Morris has brought to San Francisco. The 49ers signed edge rusher Khalid Kareem from the Falcons' Practice Squad before the season opener. Atlanta selected Trice with the 74th overall pick in the third round of the 2024 NFL Draft out of Washington, hoping he could develop into a productive pass rusher. However, his professional career got off to a difficult start when he tore his ACL during his first preseason game as a rookie. Trice missed the entire 2024 season before suffering another setback with the same knee during the 2025 campaign. Those injuries kept him out of a regular-season game during his first two years with the organization. The 25-year-old entered training camp healthy in 2026 but did not make Atlanta's initial 53-man roster. After clearing waivers, he returned to the Falcons' practice squad in early September. Atlanta gave Trice three weeks of practice squad elevations to prove himself. His Week 3 performance against the Green Bay Packers stood out, as he recorded four quarterback hurries while helping Atlanta's defensive front generate pressure. The Falcons eventually signed Trice to their active roster on Oct. 17 after using all three of his standard practice squad elevations. However, his time back on the 53-man roster was brief, as Atlanta released him three days later after the Falcons signed Charles Snowden from the Washington Commanders Practice Squad . Trice appeared in four games for Atlanta this season, recording two total tackles and one pass defended, according to the Falcons' official release announcement and NFL statistics. He also showed flashes as a pass rusher, particularly with his four quarterback hurries against Green Bay. For San Francisco, the visit offers a chance to evaluate a young defender who has faced significant adversity but is finally getting meaningful NFL playing time. His experience working along the defensive front could give the 49ers another option as they assess their depth at linebacker and edge defender. Morris' presence adds an interesting connection between Trice's former team and his potential next destination, even without a previous on-field relationship between the two. Trice has yet to establish himself as a consistent NFL contributor, but his healthy return in 2026 gave him his first chance to show the ability that earned him a third-round selection. Whether that opportunity continues in San Francisco remains to be seen. picks.blurb: Morris is surely equipped to counter Atlanta's attack, having led the same core from 2024-25 as head coach. But a San Francisco defense that tops the league in defensive expected points added per play on rushing attempts will be in for its stiffest test yet against the All-Pro ball carrier. On the other side of the ball, Brock Purdy will look to maintain sky-high efficiency despite mounting attrition at wide receiver . Falcons vs 49ers odds, moneyline, over/under Opening lines: Spread: 49ers -4.5 Moneyline: 49ers -230; Falcons +190 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Falcons vs 49ers USA TODAY expert picks Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: 49ers 35, Falcons 24 How San Francisco's surprising defense handles Robinson is sure to be one of the most compelling storylines in this game. But mitigating any damage might not fall on that unit alone. Chicago managed to minimize Robinson's role by stringing together long drives and holding onto the ball for more than 40 minutes. Given how prolific San Francisco's offense is at working the intermediate area - and how badly Atlanta's defense struggles in that area - the 49ers could leave the Falcons in a problematic position by racing out to an early lead and controlling the terms of the game. Adam Kaufman: 49ers 30, Falcons 23 At some point, San Francisco's injuries have to catch up with it, right? The 49ers keep answering that question with another win to stay unbeaten, although Mike Evans' latest injury creates another challenge on a short week before traveling to Atlanta. Fortunately, Brock Purdy still has Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle to help keep the offense moving. I like those options against a Falcons secondary that has struggled. The Falcons' path is straightforward: feed Bijan Robinson, keep Purdy watching and prevent Michael Penix Jr. from having to rescue the game with difficult throws. That should keep Atlanta competitive, but I'm still expecting San Francisco to execute more consistently and take advantage of a mistake or two. Will McFadden Senior Reporter FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. — The Atlanta Falcons will look to break their two-game skid against one of the NFL's three remaining undefeated teams when the San Francisco 49ers come to town for a 1 p.m. ET kickoff on Sunday. Injuries have become a storyline for both teams, particularly for Atlanta's defense and San Francisco's offense, and there could be some important game-time decisions. Nevertheless, there is plenty of familiarity between these coaching staffs and star power on these rosters. As was the case in Week 5, when the Falcons faced the Baltimore Ravens, this game will feature two of the league's preeminent running backs in Bijan Robinson and Christian McCaffrey. The 49ers are also led offensively by quarterback Brock Purdy, who is playing arguably the best football of his career so far this season. "The more you watch him, the more you just appreciate the player that he is," Falcons defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich said of Purdy. "He does everything well. And that's the truth. His footwork, he's getting through his progressions, his timing, his accuracy, the velocity he puts on the ball, the touch. And then when it's all said and done, the ability to create when it's not there." Purdy could be missing his top target on Sunday, though, as Mike Evans left the 49ers' last game before halftime due to injury. Atlanta's defense could get a key player of its own back for this one as A.J. Terrell Jr. began practicing this week after spending the last four games on injured reserve due to a groin injury. If both players suit up on Sunday, Terrell and Evans will rekindle a familiar matchup. Here's a look at who the experts predict will win on Sunday between the Falcons and 49ers. away.blurb: Cornerback A.J. Terrell was back at practice after being designated to return from the injured reserve list. Terrell, who's been on IR for the last four weeks, was a limited participant at Wednesday's practice. Atlanta's top cornerback has a chance to play this week against the San Francisco 49ers. Surprisingly, Falcons rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels was a full participant to being NFL Week 7. Daniels was taken to the hospital after suffering a neck injury in Week 6. The fourth-round out of Oklahoma also seemingly has a chance to play Sunday. Falcons edge rushers Za'Darius Smith and Samson Ebukam were among the nine players limited to begin the practice week. away.headline: 49ers week 7 injury report is bad news for WR Mike Evans
away.blurb: There are a handful of players already ruled out for Week 7, but we could see some players back in action against the Falcons as the 49ers look to get a little healthier in time to go for a 7-0 start to the 2026 campaign. 49ers Week 7 injury report: Mike Evans among 6 ruled out It's not a surprise Evans is out while he deals with Achilles tendinitis, but Shanahan used the same language about the injury for Week 7 that he did leading up to Week 6 when Evans suited up despite not practicing. After Evans left Week 6 late in the first half and with the bye week lingering it behooves the 49ers to shut the 33-year-old receiver down. This will be the first game Evans misses with the 49ers. Christian Kirk trending toward return in Week 7 It's not a huge surprise to see optimism about Kirk's return for the 49ers' game in Atlanta. With Mike Evans potentially out because of Achilles tendinitis San Francisco needs reinforcements. Kirk's practice window was opened before Week 6, and now with a second week of practice in it sounds like the club is gearing up for him to come back in Week 7. Head coach Kyle Shanahan on Thursday spoke with KNBR and said Kirk is trending toward making his 2026 debut. " He looked good out there ," Shanahan said. "Talking to him he felt good, and I think he felt good last week. So it's trending in the right direction." The 49ers only open the first portion of practice to media, and neither Bosa nor Evans were on hand for the open part of the session according to reporters on site. Evans is working through Achilles tendonitis. He didn't practice leading up to Week 6 and still suited up before exiting the game late in the second quarter. For Bosa there was optimism he'd be back Thursday. Early indications are he isn't going to participate, but that could change if he comes out after media exit. Kyle Shanahan hopes Nick Bosa will return to practice Thursday Bosa has been out since Week 3 when he suffered a calf injury. The issue wasn't supposed be long-term and there was some hope he'd return for Week 6. Bosa didn't practice at all in Week 6 before being ruled out. He didn't participate in Wednesday's session, but head coach Kyle Shanahan expressed some optimism the star defensive end would be in the team's second practice of the week. "Can't go today, but hoping he'll be out there tomorrow," Shanahan said before practice. There may not be a team in the NFL more in need of a Bye week than the San Francisco 49ers . San Francisco will visit the Atlanta Falcons in Week 7, and then they'll be off for Week 8 where their injury situation could improve dramatically. We'll be keeping a close eye on the 49ers' injury updates all week. home.headline: Bears report card: How we graded Chicago in Week 6 win vs. Falcons
home.blurb: Chicago’s defense was outstanding in this game. However, after giving up just one measly touchdown in the first three quarters, they started to unravel a bit in the fourth after their starters were pulled up 31-7. The positive side of the B comes from how well they played, but it’s not an A because of the door cracking open for Atlanta in the final frame. Kyler Gordon made his return from injury, which made this his season debut. It seemed like there was some off-the-field drama with his absence, but like most of these types of stories, they’re overblown. He looked ready to go in a big way once he stepped on the field. In addition to making four tackles, Gordon had three sacks and two forced fumbles. He could play this well again in every game and still not have stats like that. It’s looking like a big boost to their group going forward. Chicago’s defense needed a spark in the defensive backfield and with their pass rush. They didn’t expect Kyler Gordon to give them help in both areas, but that was the case in Atlanta. With the two teams that won their respective conferences last season up next, the Bears knew that getting a win in Atlanta was important. Getting to 4-2 made it so they could battle the New England Patriots and Seattle Seahawks with a bit more confidence. The Bears are becoming known as an offensive team, but the defense has left a lot to be desired. In this win on Sunday, everybody did enough to make sure they got on the flight home with the win. Here's how we graded every unit after the Week 6 victory. The Bears offense scored 31 points. Caleb Williams retur4ned from an injury and dominated as well as he ever has in the NFL. He completed 30-of-36 passes for 305 yards and a touchdown. Colston Loveland caught the lone touchdown pass, and it was his best overall game because of his six total catches on seven targets. Luther Burden caught all eight of his receptions for a total of 95 yards. Outside of those two, the ball was equally spread around. If Williams thinks you can help advance the ball, he’ll throw it to you. In the run game, without Kyle Monangai, the Bears did just enough with D’Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson. Between them, they had three rushing touchdowns, which played key roles in the win. The Bears special teams units were incredible in this game. Cairo Santos missed a 56-yard field goal, but they probably shouldn’t have put him in that position anyway. He was nails on every other attempt. They had plenty of good field position thanks to returns by Zavion Thomas and Kalif Raymond, but their punting unit also made some noise. Between causing two turnovers and pinning the Falcons deep, they did a great job. This is one of the rare special teams A-grades for doing more than just “not messing things up”. The offense and the defense had things easier on Sunday thanks to special teams. The Bears coaching staff came very close to getting an A. Can a previously 0-5 squad keep pushing the turnaround and secure their second straight victory? Last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts represented a new wave of promise for the Titans. But in the Browns, Tennessee will face the top team (in a three-way tie) in the AFC North. Cleveland has come on strong, and are coming to Nashville off a 13-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens. In the wake of a long-awaited win, I've got one reason the Titans will beat the Browns, one reason they won't, as well as my own prediction. Will: Robert Saleh's defense takes over again Robert Saleh's defense just had their best performance of the season. Almost single-handedly, the score-stopping unit bottled up the Colts' offense when it mattered. The Titans forced multiple turnovers and forced Daniel Jones to make mistakes through the air. If Tennessee finds a way to win again this week, it will likely be due to a similar performance from the defense. Expect Saleh to send the heat once again after last week's six-sack outing. PFF has the Browns' offensive line ranked all the way down at 26th in the NFL. If the Titans' defensive line can force Deshaun Watson to unsettle in the pocket, we could be in for a similar path to victory for Tennessee. Won't: Browns get young playmakers going Oppositely, with the Titans' offense still operating at an inconsistent level, this game could get out of hand if Cleveland gets their young playmakers going. If the Browns come out swinging, and the Titans' offense takes as long as usual to get into any kind of rhythm, the team could be facing another steep halftime deficit. I just don't like their odds to overcome that two weeks in a row, even if this game is in Nashville. Prediction: Titans win, 17-14 However, I don't believe the Titans will have to worry about that. I'll err to to the positive side with my prediction (something I could be accused of doing too often) and say that Saleh's defense has another big game on the way to a Titans win. This team hasn't won two straight games since Weeks 10 and 11 of the 2022 season. That's a vile streak, but after last week's victory, now feels like the perfect time for Tennessee to break it. Saleh finally has his legs under him as a head coach with this team. The Browns haven't scored more than 13 points in two weeks. In front of a potentially revamped home crowd, the stars are aligning for a home upset for Tennessee. I don't believe the offense will take any major strides, but in Week 7, maybe they won't have to. I predict a narrow Titans win over the Browns. Published Oct 21, 2026 LANE MILLS Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. LeBron's biggest comeback 3 Bold predictions for the Browns against the Titans in Week 7 Andrew Harbaugh, Browns Wire Wed, October 21, 2026 at 2:55 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Cleveland Browns march into Week 7 with an AFC North division lead and momentum behind them again. They are starting a softer stretch of the schedule but remain focused on the task ahead, which is the Tennessee Titans. Despite winning their first game in Week 6, the Titans are better than they have played. The Browns can win this game, though, if they keep up their defensive aggressiveness and make significant second-half adjustments. Todd Monken and his staff have risen to the occasion in every game, but this could be their first complete game in 2026 if they execute the way they are capable of. We said this is a poor Titans team, but there is still a game to be played, and we have some bold predictions to share ahead of it. Jared Verse gets his first sack of the season This is a wild thing to think about, but heading into Week 7 against the Tennessee Titans, Jared Verse is without a sack this season. Equally, Myles Garrett has also gone without a sack, but he has been on injured reserve. Fair or unfair, Verse is going to be linked to Garrett, and that means expectations will always be high. The Titans' offensive line is not the best unit, they are going to give up pressures, and it is time for Verse to capitalize on that. Jerry Jeudy finds the endzone Jerry Jeudy has seen him get more and more reps and big-time targets since Week 4 against the Pittsburgh Steelers. In Week 6, he made a pivotal catch-and-run that set up the game-winning field goal by Andre Szmyt. Deshaun Watson and Todd Monken have spoke highly of Jeudy this past week and he seems poised for another boost to his role. In Week 7 against he Titans, he can take advantage of their poor secondary and find the endzone for the first time this season. Browns secure at least five sacks Titans quarterback Cam Ward has had a rough start to the season and it has Tennessee sitting with a record of 1-5. He has a tendency to hold onto the ball, be reckless with it, and I think that has the Browns poised to have a big week on the defensive side of the ball. You cannot always count on turnovers, but you can count on Mike Rutenberg being aggressive on defense. One way he will do that is by getting after Ward, and I think that is where the Browns are most productive in the form of securing at least five sacks. picks.blurb: NFL predictions: With the defense cooking, will the Browns-Titans matchup be put to bed early? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football World Series preview NFL injury updates Knicks change ring tune Cowboys not trading? LeBron's biggest comeback Chris Pokorny Sat, October 24, 2026 at 12:14 AM UTC · 10 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads This Sunday, the Cleveland Browns (4-2) take on the Tennessee Titans (1-5). Below, we analyze a few advantages, disadvantages, or general thoughts about the two teams before getting to our predictions for the game. Browns' Defense is Cooking… …except for the start of football games. In four of their six games, including their last three games, this has been the result of the opposing team's opening drive: Week 1, Jaguars: 8 plays, 59 yards (Touchdown) Week 4, Steelers: 17 plays, 73 yards (Touchdown) Week 5, Jets: 8 plays, 90 yards (Touchdown) Week 6, Ravens: 11 plays, 66 yards (Touchdown) In that first game, the defense was just bad the whole first half. In the other three games, they did a pretty solid-to-dominant job the rest of the way. I've harped a bunch of times this season on how much I value the adjustments that Mike Rutenburg has this defense making in-game, which is something I thought I never saw from Jim Schwartz . We're also seeing where a defensive front is not reliant on one guy ( Myles Garrett ) to save the day. Players are collectively stepping up and rallying together, and you're also seeing great individual efforts out of the likes of Denzel Ward , Carson Schewesinger , and Maliek Collins . This week, the Browns get Mason Graham back, who looked like a beast to begin his second year before hurting his knee. With the defense playing so well, it's also encouraging this week that they are facing the 32nd-ranked offense in the NFL. Cam Ward hasn't been able to muster much in the passing game. Also last year, RB Tony Pollard had his best game of the season against Cleveland, going off for 161 yards on 25 carries with 2 touchdowns. Hopefully, that element can be contained, especially with help returning at defensive tackle. But the Offense Needs to do More The fourth quarter, game-winning drives have happened four times this season, which is great on one hand. It almost happened a fifth time (the loss to the Jets). On the other hand, we're starting to reach a bit of a tipping point on needing to see more productivity and points on the board in the rest of the game. Over those first few games of the season, the feeling was, 'Alright, we're seeing some encouraging things, maybe as the offense continues to build a rhythm, we'll see better results.' Instead, things have gotten pretty stagnant from an overall game perspective. Cleveland has scored 12 and 13 points in their last two games, fortunate to have gone 1-1 during that stretch. Over the last three weeks, Cleveland is the only team to have a victory on the board after scoring that few of points. The last team that won with that low of a point total was the Giants back in Week 3, when they won 12-7 over…the Titans. In other words, Cleveland was lucky to scoot by with a victory in that sense last week, and if their offense is not better, even against the Titans, you're going to have teams beating you. What can get better? Last week, one of the adjustments seems to have been getting Jerry Jeudy more involved in the game again. The running game also showed some progress, but ironically enough, many fans feel that was because Quinshon Judkins was out, and Jaleel McLaughlin was back. I'm not trying to be a Judkins hater by any means — like I've said multiple times, I thought he looked very sharp last year, and this year, I think he looks as pedestrian as you can get. Dylan Sampson might also return this week. Something is off that KC Concepcion is six games in, and has 186 yards receiving (average of 31 yards receiving per game). I go back to what I saw from him in training camp, and I know that was just training camp, but my takeaway multiple times was, ' This guy is something special.' And it's also not like I say that about every receiver that comes through the team because I'm a homer. I don't think I've ever felt that about a receiver in camp. And during the regular season, I think he's looked the part still — it's just, tying in with the rest of the offense, the production isn't there yet. Harold Fannin , also, has 2 catches for 13 yards in the last two games. The Titans have defended tight ends fairly well this year, so I don't know if there's a breakout to be expected this week, but the young tight end needs to get involved more. Tennessee picked up their first win of the season last week, but their offense didn't find themselves. They were shut out 13-0 at the half, then forced a fumble, got an interception (which both led to field goals), and then blocked a punt for a touchdown, to generate points. That should be a talking point for the Browns this week, but if they protect the ball and are diligent about special teams assignments like they've been, Tennessee's offense shouldn't beat them. According to FanDuel , the Browns are 1.5 point favorites against the Titans. The over/under is 37.5. Quick Hitters Offensive coordinator Travis Switzer was asked about getting his top two running backs returning this week: Yeah, it's huge. I mean, it's obviously our top two backs. So, yeah, those two are a big part of what we do on offense, run and pass. And they're also, we talked about this last week too, a little bit of a one-two punch, if you will, whatever you want to call it. They have different skill sets that we can utilize for both of them. So, yeah, having those guys back is going to be huge. Defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg talked about Emmanuel McNeil-Warren getting a lot of action last week after Grant Delpit exited early: I mean, he did a great job in the game. Was excellent with his communication, was excellent with his assignments, and then you saw his playmaking ability come to life. But that goes back to him continuing to build his confidence. You saw it earlier in the year on special teams, playing really, really well on special teams, getting more opportunities on defense, playing really well in practice, and him transferring that to the game. And he's going to continue going this way because of, number one, just who he is. He wants to be coached, he wants the information, he wants to be challenged, he wants to be told when it's good, when it's bad. And then you can see his play continuing to rise because of who he is. Special teams coordinator Bryon Storer was asked about Corey Bojorquez not having his best game last week: "Yeah, I mean, we didn't think it was, he could have…He had more opportunities that he could have taken advantage of. It's the minus, the two minus-45 kicks, where you're like, we've got to have those balls inside the 20-yard line. And that's what I told him after the game, looking at it, it's like, 'we've got to get the ball inside the 20 on those', because if you get the ball inside the 20 on those, you've got four inside the 20 for the game. And you only gave up, I think it was like 7.5 yards per return, and so if you handled those punts better, you're looking at the game completely differently. But we talked about it, and really just trying to keep the ball from going out of bounds so early, because you leave it up to the official to mark wherever he thinks it goes out. Now, I think there is some technology to it now that we learned, but he's got to do a better job of keeping it in play. And we've proven now with Malachi (Corley) that we can down the punt inside the 10-yard line. So, I think we learned from that and we'll see improvement from us." Here are predictions from multiple staff members at DBN: Chris Pokorny: "Many are predicting this to be a close game, with Cleveland squeaking out a win. I can't blame them, considering the Browns' four victories have been by a combined 13 points. But with the momentum the Browns continue to build, I feel like their defense is rocking with confidence this week, and the offense finds a slight groove to make this a double digit win." Browns 27, Titans 10 Jared Mueller : "A road game with a bit of weird attached to it with the Jordan Elliott release from the Titans and his history with the Browns. This seems similar to the game versus the Jets; the Browns seem to stay close to their opponent for a variety of reasons, and can struggle to put things away. Tennessee is coming off their first victory and a young team can get on a roll quickly. If Quincy Williams' neck injury leads to him missing the game, Cleveland's defense all of a sudden has a big, important question mark. As of now, the weather looks like it will be perfect in Nashville, with a high of 77 degrees. That will help the Browns offense get going a bit." Browns 24, Titans 20 Curtiss Brown: "The last time these two teams played, Cleveland couldn't stop the run for whatever reason. The Titans aren't an abject disaster but its hard to say this team has looked better than last year. A case can be made they look worse. However, the team was able to get a win against the Indianapolis Colts so they aren't completely bad. As for the Browns, its hard to say that they are a good football team. They aren't bad but they aren't necessarily good. Mediocre at best is fine. The Titans will give this team fits (mainly on defense) but the Browns defense has to be prepared for quarterback Cam Ward. If the offense can find some consistency and play a complete game that would be nice. Could be a close game but Cleveland barely wins. I could be wrong though." Browns 23, Titans 20 Barry Shuck: "After the schedule came out, I looked at the Browns opponents. They are playing that last place schedule, which means, except for the Cardinals and Dolphins, they play every division cellar dweller from last year. I looked at what Todd Monken had done with virtually every offensive unit he has been charged of. Every single team's offense improved tremendously. So, I predicted Cleveland could take the bad teams, split within the division, then come out with a 12-5-0 record. However, one of those wins was supposed to the Jets. And after a 2-4-0 start, the Jets remain a bad team. This brings up the Titans, who just might be the worst team in the league. Which, the Browns should win, right? My memory still is on how Cleveland gave up their soul against New York, and floundered. A 38-14 win for the Browns? Or a 17-13 heartbreaker to a horrible club instead? Which offense shows up?" The total in this game currently sits at 37.5 over at FanDuel Sportsbook . That is the lowest total of the week, and the under might be the smart bet. The Titans are last in the league in yards per game at 236.3. The Browns are 29th at 267.5. Get ready for a lot of punts. The key for the Titans in this game will be taking care of the ball. Last week, the Titans forced three turnovers against the Indianapolis Colts. That, and a couple of key special teams plays, were the difference in the game. Dike was the biggest weapon the Titans had last season, but he had struggled this season before last week. Hopefully, that was the start of his return to the All-Pro returner he was last season. This game does feature two good rookie wide receivers. Denzel Boston leads all rookie receivers with 345 yards and is averaging over 20 yards per catch. Carnell Tate is right behind him with 344 yards. If one of those guys can break a big play, it could be the difference in this game. Don't expect a thrilling game when you sit down to watch this one on Sunday, but if the Titans can play a game similar to the one they did last week, they might have a chance at back-to-back wins for the first time since 2022.

home.headline: Wednesday injury report for the Browns in Week 7 against the Titans
home.blurb: As Wednesday's opening injury report dropped, Cleveland finds itself navigating another long list of bumps and bruises. Six players were sidelined to start the week, while a heavy group of eight contributors were managed with limited workloads. He was joined on the sideline by starting center Elgton Jenkins (knee) and linebacker Carson Schwesinger (ankle). Interior defensive line depth remains an area to watch as Kalia Davis and Mike Hall Jr. both sat out, while backup guard Teven Jenkins remains sidelined with a back injury. Eight players logged limited reps on Wednesday. Starting running back Quinshon Judkins and defensive tackle Mason Graham both maintained limited workloads as they work through lingering lower-body issues. Rookie wideout KC Concepcion was managed with calf and quad injuries, while fellow rookie receiver Denzel Boston, right tackle Tytus Howard, edge rusher Derek Barnett, and running back Dylan Sampson were also held to limited participation. The Vikings are 5-0 on the season and 4-1 against the spread, only failing to cover as -9.5 favorites in a 15-10 win over the Dolphins. On the other hand, the Colts fell to 2-4 last week with an upset loss to the previously winless Titans. It was their second straight loss after a 34-22 defeat in Pittsburgh on Oct. 11. Using the latest odds and analysis, here’s where I’m leaning for this Week 7 matchup with a final score prediction. And you can only beat who you’re scheduled to play. Minnesota deserves to be this big of a favorite out of its bye against the Colts. picks.blurb: NFL Week 7 Survivor Pool Picks (Vikings Over Colts, Jets in AFC East Duel Highlight Top Predictions) Skip to main content ON SI PREDICTION MARKETS Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI Another week, another bloodbath for Survivor Pools. It seems like every week a big favorite is being upset, and Week 6 had two of them as the Los Angeles Rams (12.5-point favorites) lost outright at home to the Arizona Cardinals while the Indianapolis Colts (seven-point favorites) lost an AFC South battle with the previously winless Tennessee Titans. So, if you’re still alive in Survivor heading into Week 7, you deserve a ton of credit. The SI Betting team was banged up in Week 6, as managing editor Peter Dewey came up short with his Colts pick. On the bright side, those of our readers that tailed senior editor Iain MacMlllam, the New England Patriots improved to 19-2 in their last 21 home games against the New York Jets with a victory on Sunday. The Patriots have won three games in a row and are suddenly back in the mix to earn the top seed in the AFC this season. Week 7 doesn’t feature a ton of obvious Survivor spots, as the Houston Texans (9.5-point favorites against the New York Giants), Minnesota Vikings (5.5-point favorites against the Colts) and Rams (5.5-point favorites against the Las Vegas Raiders) are the three teams favored by the most on Sunday. So, Survivor players are going to have to at least consider a closer game to keep themselves alive. Here’s a quick recap of the Week 6 picks before we share our Week 7 selections. NFL Week 6 Survivor Picks Recap Peter Dewey: Indianapolis Colts (L) Iain MacMillan: New England Patriots (W) It wasn’t a perfect week in these picks, but as always we’ll allow Dewey to “buy back in” so we can share differing perspectives each week in these picks. Week 7 may be the toughest week of the season, as some quality teams (Buffalo, Jacksonville mainly) are on the bye. Washington and the Los Angeles Chargers also won’t play in Week 7. Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook NFL Week 7 Survivor Pool Picks New York Jets Geno Smith and the New York Jets are off to a 2-4 start, but they’ve been competent so far this season. Not only are the Jets 4-1-1 against the spread, but they rank sixth in the NFL in opponent yards per play and are 10th in EPA/Play on defense. The offense isn’t nearly as good (19th in EPA/Play, 22nd in yards per play), but the Jets have a very favorable matchup against a winless Miami Dolphins team – at home – in Week 7. Miami is coming off a bye, but it has just one game all season where it’s scored more than 13 points. The Dolphins rank 28th in EPA/Play, 27th in success rate and 22nd in yards per play allowed through five games this season. While I don’t believe either one of these squads is a playoff team, the Jets have a much higher floor with Geno Smith under center. New York has also hung around with playoff contenders like Green Bay, Detroit and New England while beating a 4-2 Cleveland team in Week 5. I have no faith in this Miami team, which seems destined for a top-three pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. Miami had a backdoor cover against the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 5, but it has relied on garbage time to get back into games that never were really close to begin with. With De’Von Achane out for the season, Malik Willis doesn’t have enough help to really get this offense going, and now he has to take on a Jets unit that has been one of the better ones in the NFL. Since the Texans are the only big favorite on the board this week – and they're just 2-4 themselves in 2026 – I don’t mind taking a shot on the Jets. I can’t imagine another spot (outside of their road game vs. Miami) where I’d really feel comfortable taking them in Survivor. – Peter Dewey Minnesota Vikings Despite the Minnesota Vikings being undefeated so far this season, this might be the last week I'd feel confident taking them. They're fresh off a bye week and have arguably the best defense in the NFL. That very same defense is going to be able to put Daniel Jones and the Indianapolis Colts' offense in a blender. It's clear by now that the key to beating the Colts is stopping Jonathan Taylor, and the Vikings rank in the top three in virtually every single run defense stat. Kyler Murray should be able to produce enough offense to let his defense lead them to a win in this interconference duel. – Iain MacMillan Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. LeBron's biggest comeback 3 Bold predictions for the Vikings against the Colts in Week 7 Cole Smith, Vikings Wire Thu, October 22, 2026 at 3:55 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Minnesota Vikings enter their Week 7 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts looking to extend the league's longest winning streak. Since Week 14 of the 2025 season, the Vikings have won 10 straight games, building a 5-0 record going into last week's bye. They face a 2-4 Indianapolis team that fired general manager Chris Ballard on Monday, one day after losing 26-20 to the previously winless Tennessee Titans. Head coach Shane Steichen is still employed , but the Colts feel combustible right now, with rumors of trading away star players like RB Jonathan Taylor and G Quenton Nelson swirling. Minnesota can't afford to overlook Indianapolis if they want to keep pace with the 6-0 San Francisco 49ers. But this feels like an opportunity for the Vikings to jump on an inferior team that is going through organizational changes. Here are three bold predictions for the Vikings when they host the Colts at U.S. Bank Stadium on Sunday. Jordan Mason will run for 100+ yards and 2 touchdowns Jordan Mason appears to return to the lineup after missing the past four games with a thumb injury that landed him on injured reserve. Kevin O'Connell told Paul Allen on Tuesday that he expects to see Mason, Jordan Addison, T.J. Hockenson, and Christian Darrisaw back at practice on Wednesday . With Mason back, Minnesota can return to its 1-2 punch with Aaron Jones. Indianapolis enters Week 7 as one of the league's worst run defenses. They rank 22nd in rushing yards allowed, but their 4.8 yards per run allowed is tied for 5th-worst in the league. Their 12.3% stuff-rate ranks 30th in the league, and they rank last in EPA/run allowed. I expect the Vikings to stay committed to the run game and give Jones some relief after he carried the ball 85 times for 370 yards from Weeks 2 to 5. Mason averaged 3.5 yards after contact per carry in 2025, tied for 11th-best in the league among qualifying running backs. I see him breaking 100 yards and reaching the end zone twice on Sunday. Jauan Jennings will catch a touchdown pass Trade rumors swirled around Jauan Jennings in the days after Minnesota's 23-13 win over the Saints in Week 5. He was caught on camera slamming his fist into the ground following Myles Price's fumble that was returned for a touchdown. That came two plays after Jennings appeared to get open for a potential touchdown, but Murray instead threw an incompletion to Tai Felton. One play later, Murray slightly overthrew Jennings in the end zone. Jennings has caught only two passes for nine yards this season, but the rumors of a potential trade seem to have died down. He's gotten open enough that he should be getting more targets, but look for him to find more separation downfield, with Justin Jefferson, Addison, and Hockenson potentially back this week. With extra attention on the other weapons on the field, Murray will make up for his red zone misses against the Saints. The Vikings will sack Daniel Jones 5+ times and pick him off multiple times This will be the first time Daniel Jones plays against the Vikings since spending the end of the 2024 season with them. He signed with the Colts last year and played well until a fractured fibula in Week 12 slowed him down, and an Achilles tear ended his season two weeks later. He completed 68% of his passes for 3,101 yards (8.1 yards per attempt), 19 touchdowns, and eight interceptions. Jones hasn't been as efficient this season, completing 59.6% of his passes and averaging 5.9 yards per attempt, with four touchdowns and six picks. He has been pressured on 42.1% of his dropbacks, tied for the league's 7th-highest mark. Of course, no one pressures quarterbacks as much as Minnesota does. They have a league-high 47.8% quarterback pressure rate, spearheaded by a 67.0% blitz rate that is 24.5 percentage points higher than the next-closest team. Look for the Vikings to get after Jones all day and force him into turnovers. This article originally appeared on Vikings Wire: 3 Bold predictions for the Vikings against the Colts in Week 7
