Vikings v. Colts on Sunday Minnesota is coming off a bye week. Indianapolis lost 26-20 at home last week to the Tennessee Titans, making it their second consecutive loss. They just fired their general manager this week and very possibly could be having a fire sale at the trade deadline (doing so would make plenty of sense). Jan 8, 2023; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Indianapolis Colts guard Quenton Nelson (56) in the first half against the Houston Texans at Lucas Oil Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Trevor Ruszkowski-USA TODAY Sports. Could either Jonathan Taylor or Quenton Nelson be traded to Minnesota? Either would be great additions. Indianapolis leads the all-time series 18-9-1 , but have lost the past two meetings. These two teams last faced each other during the 2024 season in Minnesota. Sam Darnold went 28/34 for 290 yards, three touchdowns, and two interceptions. Aaron Jones rushed for 64 yards on 21 carries. Justin Jefferson caught seven passes for 137 yards. Josh Oliver caught five passes for 58 yards and a touchdown. "The turnovers are nothing. Those are just little minor errors that we can fix easily," Jefferson said . "We've just got to protect the ball, just not try to make that big play. Sam is a phenomenal quarterback." On defense, Ivan Pace Jr recorded a team-high six tackles. Jonathan Greenard recorded two sacks. For Indianapolis, Joe Flacco went 16/27 for 179 yards and an interception. Taylor rushed for 48 yards on 13 carries. Josh Downs caught six passes for 60 yards. Dec 4, 2022; Arlington, Texas, USA; Indianapolis Colts quarterback Matt Ryan (2) hands off to running back Jonathan Taylor (28) in the first quarter against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Tim Heitman-USA TODAY Sports. On defense, E.J. Speed recorded a game-high 12 tackles. Grover Stewart recorded two sacks. Minnesota won 21-13 to improve to 6-2 on the season. They finished the season at 14-3 and made the playoffs as a wild card. They fell in the first round to the Los Angeles Rams on the road. Indianapolis fell to 4-5 with the loss. They finished the season at 8-9 and missed the playoffs for the fourth consecutive season. This is another game Minnesota should win. You can maybe call this a must-win given Indianapolis is not a good team and Minnesota's schedule gets tougher after this. Currently, the Chicago Bears, Green Bay Packers, and Detroit Lions all have two losses apiece. This should be Minnesota's division to lose at the moment, but there is still plenty of time until the regular season ends. They also have still not played Detroit and still have to play both Green Bay and Chicago one more time. As for the rest of the NFC, the San Francisco 49ers are the only other undefeated team in the conference. Despite having many injuries, San Francisco keeps on winning. They currently should be considered the best team in the NFC. The Vikings just need to keep winning and they would not have to worry too much about the rest of the division. As far as the top seed in the NFC, they need to of course keep winning, but also need San Francisco to start losing too. Sep 27, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; Minnesota Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell watches quarterback Kyler Murray (1) warm up prior to the game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images The defense has been exceptional all season. The offense has not been very good, but Kyler Murray has looked better the past two games, which is encouraging. They also are expected to have Jordan Mason, Christian Darrisaw, Jordan Addison and T.J. Hockenson back this week. Will Nolan Teasley add to the offense at the trade deadline in a few weeks ? He very likely could and should. For this team to compete for the Super Bowl, they need to improve on offense, whether it is for a running back or a left guard. Another option could be adding a blocking tight end to replace Oliver. If not offense, maybe they could try to make the defense even stronger. They could use an upgrade at safety or maybe even add a defense tackle next to Jalen Redmond. This team is very good, but can still use another move or two if they want to go far in the playoffs. First thing is first, though. They need to win this Sunday to be 6-0. Keep getting in the win column and get ready for the tougher opponents after this week. away.blurb: The Indianapolis Colts are coming off their second-straight and fourth total loss of the 2026 season, and it’s safe to say a large reason why is because they were without one of their top playmakers. Unfortunately, his return to the field remains unknown. The Colts selected Warren with the No. 14 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft out of Penn State, where he won the John Mackey Award as the nation’s top tight end in 2024. It’s certainly not the news Colts fans were hoping to hear as the team is schedule to take on the undefeated Minnesota Vikings in Week 7. However, head coach Shane Steichen did provide a bit of a promising update after practice. “He’s progressing really well, but I’ll defer to the injury report this week on a lot of those guys,” Steichen said . It can’t be understated how much Warren means to the Colts’ offense. Despite missing Week 6, he still leads the team with 30 catches to go along with 213 yards and two touchdowns. In the meantime, the Colts will have to continue relying on veteran wide receivers Josh Downs, Keenan Allen and Laquon Treadwell as well as backup tight end Mo Alie-Cox. It didn’t take Warren long to establish himself as one of the best up-and-coming tight ends in the league, either. As a rookie, Warren racked up 76 catches for 817 yards and four touchdowns. away.headline: Colts sign WR Mecole Hardman, P Thomas Morstead to practice squad; release WR Eli Pancol from practice squad
away.blurb: Hardman Jr., 5-10, 187 pounds, has played in 82 career games (28 starts) in his time with the Buffalo Bills (2025-26), Green Bay Packers (2025), Kansas City Chiefs (2019-24) and New York Jets (2023). He has compiled 178 receptions for 2,302 yards (12.9 avg.) and 16 touchdowns. Hardman Jr. has tallied 26 carries for 190 yards (7.3 avg.) and three touchdowns. He has totaled 46 kickoff returns for 1,134 yards (24.7 avg.) and one touchdown as well as 91 punt returns for 823 yards (9.0 avg.) and one touchdown. Hardman Jr. has appeared in 15 postseason contests (four starts) and has tallied 28 receptions for 292 yards (10.4 avg.) and four touchdowns. He has also recorded 13 carries for 105 yards (8.1 avg.) and one touchdown. Hardman Jr. has collected 15 kickoff returns for 334 yards (22.3 avg.) and seven punt returns for 86 yards (12.3 avg.). He won Super Bowls LIV and LVIII with the Chiefs. Hardman Jr. was originally selected by Kansas City in the second round (56th overall) of the 2019 NFL Draft out of Georgia. As a rookie, he was an Associated Press Second Team All-Pro choice (kick returner) and was named to the Pro Bowl (return specialist). His first name is pronounced MUH-cole. Morstead, 6-4, 225 pounds, has played in 272 career games in his time with the San Francisco 49ers (2025), New York Jets (2023-24, 2021), Miami Dolphins (2022), Atlanta Falcons (2021) and New Orleans Saints (2009-20). He has registered 1,004 punts for 46,863 yards (46.7 avg./41.3 net avg.) with 374 pinned inside the 20-yard line. Morstead has also totaled 263 touchbacks on kickoffs. He has appeared in 18 postseason contests and has compiled 64 punts for 2,821 yards (44.1 avg./40.8 net avg.) with 22 pinned inside the 20-yard line. Morstead has tallied 16 touchbacks on kickoffs. He won Super Bowl XLIV with New Orleans. Morstead was originally selected by the Saints in the fifth round (164th overall) of the 2009 NFL Draft out of SMU. In 2012, he was an Associated Press Second Team All-Pro choice and was named to the Pro Bowl. Pancol, 6-3, 205 pounds, was signed to the team's practice squad on September 23, 2026. He participated in the Colts' 2026 offseason program and training camp. Pancol was originally signed to the team's practice squad on November 18, 2025. He spent time with the Jacksonville Jaguars during the 2025 offseason program and training camp after originally signing with the team as an undrafted free agent on April 28, 2025, out of Duke. home.blurb: Ahead of Sunday's Week 7 game against the Minnesota Vikings , the Indianapolis Colts have ruled three players out and four others questionable. Walley was limited the final two days after not practicing on Wednesday. If he can't go, we could see Kapena Gushiken in the slot, with Cam Taylor-Britt likely starting outside in Gardner's absence. The Indianapolis Colts will miss a star player on each side of the football for Sunday's game against the Minnesota Vikings. Warren hasn't practiced all week after missing a Week 6 loss to the Tennessee Titans with a groin injury. Steichen said Wednesday that the 24-year-old was "progressing well" in his recovery. Despite missing Sunday's game, Warren still leads the Colts with 30 catches. The former Penn State star began his second NFL season with touchdowns in back-to-back games but has tallied 213 yards, dropping his average yards per catch to 7.1 from 10.8 in his rookie campaign. Will Mallory played his first game of the season in Warren's absence, collecting two catches for 20 yards. Mo Alie-Cox turned his only touch into a 1-yard touchdown, but Daniel Jones didn't target Andrew Ogletree once in 30 snaps. "I'm not really concerned," Gardner said Wednesday, per Colts.com's JJ Stankevitz . "I trust our training staff here, and like I said, it's not as bad as last year. I'm just happy that it's not the same spot." The timing is still rough for the Colts ahead of a matchup against star Vikings receiver Justin Jefferson. Yet Gardner has struggled this season, with Pro Football Focus noting that he's allowed the most yards per reception (21.7) of any cornerback. The short-handed Colts will look to hand the Vikings their first loss of the season this Sunday. The Week 7 clash starts at 1 p.m. ET on CBS.

home.headline: Vikings-Colts Second Injury Report
home.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Colts, they had some players upgraded and one added- linebacker CJ Allen. But starters Sauce Gardner, Tyler Warren, and Rigoberto Sanchez did not practice for a second straight day on Thursday, making their availability on Sunday increasingly doubtful. On Sunday, they could finally get a chance to play from ahead. Miami is 0-5 and hasn't held a lead in a single game this season. After releasing several veterans in the offseason and carrying an NFL-record $187.2 million in dead cap space, the Dolphins' ugly start isn't exactly shocking—especially after facing the San Francisco 49ers, Kansas City Chiefs, Minnesota Vikings, and Cincinnati Bengals in four of their first five games. Still, CBS Sports writer Garrett Podell believes Miami will finally take a lead when it faces the New York Jets on Sunday. "The Miami Dolphins' 2026 season is going exactly as one would expect for a franchise paying more for players not on its roster than for the players on its roster ($156 million)," Podell wrote. "They're 0-5 and have the NFL's worst scoring offense, averaging 14 points per game. "They're also just the second team in the Super Bowl era (since 1966) to not have a lead in the first five games of a season, along with the 2005 Houston Texans, per CBS Sports Research. However, they will acquire their first lead in a game of the 2026 season against the New York Jets. The Jets have the worst red zone offense (37.5%) in the NFL, and they haven't scored a touchdown on their last seven red zone trips, which spans the last three games. New York has also been outscored 100-6 in the final two minutes of the first half under Aaron Glenn. Miami will capitalize on Glenn's end-of-the-first-half mismanagement and take a lead in a game for the first time this season." The Jets have scored just three touchdowns in their last four games The Jets' late-half struggles could give Miami the opening it desperately needs. During his 23 games as Jets coach, Glenn's team has been outscored 100-6 in the final two minutes of the first half. New York has also been outscored 119-49 in the final two minutes of the second and fourth quarters combined. Not to mention, Glenn is 0-7 against AFC East opponents. For a Dolphins team that hasn't tasted a lead all season, Sunday could finally flip the script and put a little pressure on the Jets for a change.

away.headline: ‘He shouldn’t be playing,’ ‘It always goes horribly wrong’ — NFL fans push back on Buccaneers’ decision to start Baker Mayfield despite injury
away.blurb: Baker Mayfield’s expected return has some Buccaneers fans asking for another week of patience. The protective glove on his throwing hand isn’t doing much to settle their nerves. Todd Bowles said Friday that Mayfield is expected to start after missing three games with a dislocated right thumb. He remained listed as questionable despite practicing fully all three days this week. “Maybe wait 1 more week? We’re inventing new glove technology so that he can return early with an injured throwing thumb to a 1-5 team?” the fan wrote . The team’s practice reports provide some encouraging evidence for the return. Fans remain concerned about how those throws will translate once Carolina’s defense gets involved. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are preparing to get their starting quarterback back against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. At 1-5, however, some supporters question whether bringing him back now is worth it. Baker Mayfield Expected To Start Against Carolina Panthers Mayfield suffered the throwing-hand injury against Minnesota in Week 3 . Rookie Jalon Daniels has handled the starting job during his absence. The glove has become a focal point of the comeback discussion. According to the Buccaneers’ account of his preparation , it provides support to prevent the injured ligament from bending backward. Mayfield also acknowledged adjusting his release points because the glove changes his grip. That detail prompted one fan to question the urgency. Another supporter made a similar argument using Tampa Bay’s record. “Its easier to rest him another week we are 1 and [expletive] 5 theres genuinely no rush if he’s not 100%,” the supporter wrote . Fans Worry About Another Mayfield Comeback Through Injury One commenter greeted the news with sarcasm. “The Baker Mayfield playing hurt gimmick is back. Should go well just like it always does!” the fan wrote . The same user later clarified the criticism. “You’ve got me all wrong here, I agree he is hurt, the ‘gimmick’ is he always plays through injuries and it always goes horribly wrong,” the commenter added . Fantasy analyst Ian Hartitz also sounded unconvinced by the glove solution. “No reason to worry here. They ripped off one of the glove’s fingers! He’s fine! away.blurb: Three Pittsburgh Steelers have been ruled out for the team's Week 6 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday, and five more are questionable to suit up, according to the team's Friday injury report. Two wide receivers Ben Skowronek and Roman Wilson left the team's 34-22 Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts with injures and did not return — and they won't be back this week, either. Skowronek suffered a calf injury early in the second quarter, and then Wilson injured his left hand on the final offensive drive of the first half. Wilson had a large wrap on his left hand after the game. On Monday, head coach Mike McCarthy said neither player will return to active this week. Fellow wide receiver DK Metcalf was initially listed as questionable to play after missing practice on Friday with an illness, but he has now been cleared to play. Tight end Pat Freiermuth is also questionable to play after suffering a calf injury in practice on Saturday. Strong safety DeShon Elliott remains limited in practice and will not return this week. Starting cornerback Jamel Dean was ruled out last week, but might be ahead of the curve on the initial multi-week estimate for his injury. He is listed as questionable. Running back Rico Dowdle , who is recovering from a dislocated toe on his left foot, is also questionable to make his return to the lineup, as is defensive tackle Keeanu Benton , who has an ankle injury, and defensive who has an ankle injury, and defensive back Jalen Ramsey , who has played through his broken wrist the last two weeks. A beat up Steelers defensive kept Tom Brady out of the end zone for 55 minutes and Mitch Trubisky successfully replaced an injury Kenny Pickett as Pittsburgh beat the Buccaneers, 20-18 at Acrisure Stadium on Oct. 16, 2022. Pickett threw his first career touchdown pass to Najee Harris in the first quarter, but a hit from blitzing linebacker Devin White knocked him out of the game. Chris Boswell kicked two field goals and Trubisky found Chase Claypool for a six-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter to extend the Steelers lead. With 4:45 to play, Brady finally punched through a defense that was playing without T.J. Watt , Minkah Fitzpatrick , Ahkello Witherspoon , Levi Wallace and Cam Sutton with a touchdown pass to Leonard Fournette, but Devin Bush broke up the two-point conversion attempt, and Trubisky and the Pittsburgh offense ran out the clock. Defensive run game coordinator and outside linebackers coach Larry Foote had two stints with the Steelers, playing from 2002-08 and 2010-13 after the team made him a fifth-round draft pick out of Michigan. Foote was a two-time Super Bowl champion in Pittsburgh and also won a Super Bowl LV ring as a coach with Tampa in 2021. home.headline: Jaelan Phillips is out, but his injury isn’t the only puzzle Panthers have to solve
home.blurb: Canales soon clarified that Phillips will be out for Sunday’s game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers: “I know there are advantages to game plans, but this is something that we need to address and take care of.” With Phillips officially out — it’s unclear if he’ll be ready by the Panthers’ Thursday Night Football game against the Packers in Week 8 — the Panthers are missing more than a run-of-the-mill defensive starter. The 27-year-old who the Panthers signed to a four-year, $120 million contract this free agency has lived up to his billing as a premier pass rusher; he has 2.5 sacks through five games but has also added 18 total pressures in the pass rush — 24th among all edge rushers , according to Pro Football Focus. Phillips has also been stout against the run and a vocal leader his teammates praise. What’s also a result of Phillips being out? The absence of Phillips comes at the same time as reserve outside linebacker and special teams ace Thomas Incoom is also “week to week” with a calf injury. Incoom exited the Eagles in the first half and didn’t return, and as a result the Panthers needed to do a whole bunch of roster magic to fill his role on special teams. In each of the four special teams units Incoom contributes on — kick return, kick coverage, punt return, punt coverage — the Panthers needed to replace him with four different players, Canales said. Canales was asked if the Panthers will elevate anyone from the practice squad with Phillips and Incoom out, and he indicated that Nick Hampton would. The interior offensive lineman was placed on the team’s injured reserve before the season began due to a hamstring injury and is now waiting for his 21-day practice window to be activated. When asked Wednesday, Canales was vague about Christensen’s situation: “We’re just evaluating it, and you gotta figure out roster spots as well,” before adding that he has faith in the team’s current slate of IOLs. If Christensen were to return, that limits their flexibility to use the injured reserve. It’s also worth noting the Panthers have already waived someone off the injured reserve with an injury settlement — Claudin Cherelus a few weeks ago — to avoid further limitations. It’s possible, perhaps likely, that once Cherelus gets healthy, he’d re-sign with the Panthers, rejoining the squad without forcing the team to use one of its eight precious IR-elevation moves. home.headline: Baker Mayfield Injury Update Doesn't Improve Buccaneers' Odds vs. Panthers in NFL Week 7
home.blurb: On the bright side for the Bucs, it appears that starting quarterback Baker Mayfield has a chance to return in Week 7. Mayfield, who dislocated his thumb in Week 3 against the Minnesota Vikings, appears to be nearing a return to practice, as NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported ahead of Week 6 that there is "optimism" that the former No. 1 overall pick will return against the Carolina Panthers. Pelissero: There's "optimism" that Baker Mayfield (thumb) will return Week 7. While that move could be a reaction to Sunday's results after Carolina picked up a win against Philadelphia, it's also possible that oddsmakers aren't quite sold on the Bucs getting their starting quarterback to return just yet. Mayfield needs to be able to grip and throw a football at a usual level before the team is going to send him out into a regular-season game. Baker Mayfield Injury Update Doesn't Improve Buccaneers' Odds vs. Panthers in NFL Week 7 Skip to main content ON SI The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are well outside the playoff picture in the NFC through six weeks, as they're just 1-5 after an overtime loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday. Undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels was unable to do enough to get the Bucs a second win in a row, and the team is in last place in the NFC South entering Week 7. That would be a major boost to a Tampa Bay team that needs a winning streak to get back in the mix to make the playoffs. Despite the report from Pelissero, oddsmakers aren't buying the Bucs on the road against the first-place Panthers and Bryce Young. Tampa Bay opened as a three-point underdog on the road in Week 7, and it has since moved to a 3.5-point underdog in the latest odds at DraftKings Sportsbook . At 1-5, the Bucs are +570 to make the playoffs and +12500 to win the Super Bowl, making them one of the bigger long shots in the NFL through six weeks. Mayfield has appeared in just three games and didn't exactly play at a high level, completing 63.5 percent of his passes for 615 yards, two scores and two picks before suffering the thumb injury. He's also carried the ball 11 times for 65 yards and a score this season. Tampa Bay's practice report on Wednesday should provide more insight into Mayfield's status for Week 7. As for the Baltimore Ravens , their kicker is on notice. These teams meet in a Week 7 AFC North clash, and here are bold predictions for the contest. The Bengals (3-2) enter the game in last place in the division despite having a winning record. That's because the Ravens, Steelers, and surprising Browns all have a record of 4-2. It should be another battle for the Ravens and Bengals. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Joe Burrow will riddle the Ravens' defense for 3 TD passes When the Bengals are right, they are tough on offense. And they've been cooking this year, ranking No. 9 in the NFL in points per game. Burrow is connecting on 71.4% of his passes. He has 11 touchdown passes and three interceptions. Look for him to keep the momentum going this week. But Burrow needs to take care of the football, which Zac Taylor said would go a long way in helping the Bengals win, according to Cleveland.com. "The turnovers is what screams at you," Taylor said. "That leads into field position." And Taylor said Burrow and his teammates are ready for this matchup. "It's exciting," Taylor said. "I think our guys really get fired up for this game. Not that they don't get fired up for every game, but whenever we play in Baltimore in a road divisional game, it's a fun one to get up for, and our guys will be up for it." Bengals RB Chase Brown will score two TDs One of them will be on the receiving end of a pass from Burrow. Brown will have a nice day, despite being caught in a time share with Samaje Perine, according to The Athletic. "I think we'll continually assess how that touch share between (Perine) and Chase Brown should play out," Bengals offensive coordinator Pitcher told Geoff Hobson of Bengals.com. "Every game's different. What type of scheme we lean into is going to factor into that. Obviously, what we ran more of yesterday leans into what Samaje does well, which is get downhill and run through contact." The Bengals haven't forgotten about their ground game. "You strive for balance when it comes to run-pass," Pitcher said. "You're always wanting to be the most balanced and versatile version of yourselves. It's like those are high-level goals that you set out to attain. But never in any given situation are we going to let a high-level theoretical goal get in the way of what it means on Sunday to win a game and what is the feedback we're getting in a game on a given Sunday." Derrick Henry will rush for 80-plus yards and a TD Henry is still smarting from last week's fumble that led to the Ravens' loss to the Browns. He took blame for the game-changing turnover , according to ESPN. "I got to take care of the ball," he said. "There's no excuses for that. I got to be better. I put the team in harm's way. I sound like a broken record with this, but I got to go back to work on it. Can't put the team in that situation." Teammate Kyle Hamilton took up for Henry. "Obviously, he's Derrick Henry, Hall of Fame running back [who] wants to hold onto the ball," Hamilton said. "He knows that. He's his harshest critic, so I'm not going to say anything ill about it. He's put us in position to win a lot of games." All of this will motivate Henry for a big game against the Bengals Ravens WR Ja'Kobi Lane will catch 5 passes and score a TD Lane looked ready to roll against the Browns in his return from injury. And he should be able to carve out a significant role in Week 7. Lane looked great in training camp. The injury short-circuited his 2026 season. But now he's back in the mix. His overall stat line could be impacted if Tyler Huntley is still at quarterback. But if Jackson is back, this could be a breakout game for Lane. Who will win the game? The Bengals should be able to outscore the Ravens in this matchup. But the key factor is Jackson. If he's back, the Ravens have a much better chance of winning. But we will still roll with Burrow, Chase, and Tee Higgins having a big game, along with Brown doing his thing. Bleacher Report • 9h Bears TE Out for Season Bleacher Report • 13h Jaylen Brown Calls Out Tatum 🧢 Buffalo Bills linebacker Sam Franklin Jr. will be eligible to play in Week 8 when the team returns from a bye after having his discipline reduced. Michael Signora, NFL senior vice president of football and international communications, announced on Friday that Franklin's appeal of his one-game suspension was reduced to a $14,926 fine for unsportsmanlike conduct by hearing officer James Thrash. The NFL announced on Wednesday that Franklin was being suspended for one game due to "an act of unsportsmanlike conduct" during Buffalo's 33-30 win over the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 6. Franklin was said to have spit on a Raiders player during an extra-point attempt late in the fourth quarter. In a post on Instagram after the league announced its discipline, Franklin denied any wrongdoing: "Not a dirty player what so ever! Will always defend myself though. Still won't spit on anyone!" "As we said from the start, Sam did not and would never spit at an opponent, and there was no evidence that he did," Franklin's agents said in a statement . "We're glad the suspension was overturned and grateful to the hearing officer for a fair and thorough review. "It's unfortunate the league suspended Sam in the first place based on an unsupported accusation that received so much undeserved attention, and we hope the outcome is covered just as widely. We also hope the league takes a serious look at the opposing player's conduct, including striking Sam in the groin twice during the game. We're glad this is behind him, so Sam can get back to focusing on his teammates and next Sunday." Franklin was one of two Bills players disciplined for their actions during the Raiders game. C.J. Gardner-Johnson was suspended one game for spitting in the direction of Raiders tight end Brock Bowers. Officials flagged Gardner-Johnson for unsportsmanlike conduct and he was ejected from the game as a result of the incident. He issued an apology on social media following the Bills' win. Franklin is in his second season with the Bills after originally joining their practice squad in August 2025. He has appeared in 23 consecutive games since the start of last season. And the pieces could certainly be in place for the Texans to make that third consecutive win become a reality. Their offense is looking the best it has all season after another strong performance from C.J. Stroud. The defense will have the task of facing a new starting quarterback on the other side in J.J. McCarthy , and all of that coming back on Houston's home field tends to make their chances look even better. And when looking at the Texans' betting odds heading into Week 7, it's becoming pretty clear that the sportsbooks have one obvious favorite in mind for this weekend's action in Houston. Texans Already Projected to Rout the Giants in Week 7 According to recent odds from FanDuel Sportsbook , the Texans are now listed as 10.5-point favorites (-550 ML) over the Giants in Week 7. That's by far the Texans' highest spread heading into any week they've played this season. And when looking around the league's Week 7 matchups, Houston is currently the only team listed as a favorite by more than a touchdown––let alone being a favorite by double digits. Houston and New York have an over-under sitting at 43.5, which comes in tied for bottom-five among the NFL in terms of projected totals for Week 7. The projected point-total for these two teams doesn't look favorable for the Giants either. Houston and New York have an over-under sitting at 43.5, which comes in tied for bottom-five among the NFL in terms of projected totals for Week 7. So if the Texans are projected to win by double-digits, and the total score isn't expected to reach above 43 points, that's not much of an optimistic statement from the books on how this Giants offense could fare against a Houston defensive unit that many considered among the best in the NFL heading into this season. Will the Texans Actually Dominate the Giants as Expected? Now, projections are one thing. Clearly, the consensus is starting to lean in one clear direction for this one between the Texans and the Giants. But does Houston actually have what it takes to make that double-digit victory come to fruition? Really, it all relies upon the defense. Last game against the Jacksonville Jaguars showed that the Texans' offense is starting to get into a bit of a rhythm . A ton of receivers are getting involved and making plays, the run game showed signs of life against one of the best rushing defenses in the NFL, and the offensive line even held up to zero sacks. But the Texans' defense just hasn't been as consistently elite as this team proved to be last year. That's not saying they can't find their way back to that level–– because the personnel looks virtually identical to last year outside of a select few changes. But we still need to see Houston have multiple strong weeks defensively to really have this level of confidence in their chances on Sunday. After all, the Giants have won three games as is this season. That's more than the Texans can claim for themselves, and New York sits atop the NFC East because of it. So as 10.5-point underdogs, they seem just a slight bit underrated here, simply when considering Houston's inconsistencies on defense. Maybe the Texans wind up crushing those projections anyways, but perhaps the Giants can make this game just a little bit more interesting than the odds tend to show. away.headline: Texans will be without star RB for Giants game
away.blurb: David Montgomery out for Texans vs. Giants Pitre previously sat out Week 6, while Blankenship sustained a concussion during the team’s London game. Additionally, offensive tackle Blake Fisher is not expected to play as he nurses a thumb injury while wearing a cast. The Houston Texans beat the Jacksonville Jaguars 34-31 in London last week, with kicker Ka’imi Fairbairn converting both field-goal tries and all four extra points. They brought a long injury list home with them. Houston now turns its attention to the New York Giants. Several Texans stayed off the practice field Thursday, and the absences touched the backfield, the secondary and the offensive line. The Giants have their own concerns, with three offensive tackles missing Wednesday’s session. Houston has one more practice Friday to change any statuses. KPRC 2 Houston’s Aaron Wilson reported what Thursday’s report means for Sunday. MORE: Bold predictions in NFL Week 7: Jahmyr Gibbs, Ja’Marr Chase & more Houston Texans running back David Montgomery will miss Sunday’s game against the New York Giants due to a groin injury (h/t Aaron Wilson of KPRC2). Montgomery is set to miss his second consecutive game after exiting early during the Week 5 victory over the Tennessee Titans. He will not be the only player sidelined for the matchup. The Texans are also expected to be without nickel Jalen Pitre and safety Reed Blankenship, both of whom missed practice alongside Montgomery. MORE: 4 best Jonathan Taylor landing spots at NFL trade deadline How the Texans plan to replace Montgomery against the Giants Woody Marks is in line to lead the backfield again after gaining 56 yards on 15 carries and 25 yards on two catches against the Jaguars. Jawhar Jordan, elevated from the practice squad, added 43 rushing yards and a touchdown on six carries. Wide receiver Tank Dell is on track to make his season debut after returning from injured reserve, head coach DeMeco Ryans said Monday, per Wilson. Dell has not played since tearing multiple knee ligaments in December 2024. Tackle Trent Brown was a full participant Thursday, and tight end Dalton Schultz returned to practice. Those returns help along the offensive line and at tight end as Houston hosts the Giants on Sunday.

away.headline: Texans Injury Report vs. Giants: 3 Starters Ruled Out, Tank Dell Update
away.blurb: And for both sides, it seems like there's due to be some key absences to take note of. In the case of the Texans specifically, there appears to be three starters that will be missing out of the action this Sunday. RB David Montgomery: OUT (groin) S Reed Blankenship: OUT (concussion/hand) WR Tank Dell: QUESTIONABLE (knee) As for those who will be out for their second-straight game, that's none other than versatile defensive back Jalen Pitre, as well as veteran running back David Montgomery . Each will be out of the mix with their respective injuries––albeit minor ones––and will have their next chance to return to the lineup after the bye in Week 9. But the Texans will also be dealing with a couple of new injuries. Starting safety Reed Blankenship will be out for this one as he's still in concussion protocol, but also suffering from a hand issue that will keep him on the sidelines as well. Blankenship left the Texans' last game against the Jaguars in the middle of the first half due to injury, and would inevitably not return to the action. Now for Week 7, that absence within Houston's secondary will continue, and thus leave M.J. Stewart as the most likely fill-in at strong safety next to Calen Bullock. Along with Blankenship, the Texans are also dealing with a new absence to backup offensive tackle Blake Fisher, who's suffering from a thumb injury that doesn't seem to be a serious one given that he hasn't been placed on injured reserve, though will keep him out for this Sunday against New York. While not a starting piece of Houston's offensive front, this offense does like to roll out Fisher as a part of their jumbo packages on that side of the ball, as he's been on the field for over 60 snaps through the first five weeks. One piece of good news for the Texans, however, is the fact that wide receiver Tank Dell has officially been upgraded to questionable. LB Tremaine Edmunds: OUT (shoulder) CB Greg Newsome II: OUT (concussion) TE Theo Johnson: DOUBTFUL (neck) CB Paulson Adebo: QUESTIONABLE (knee) RT Jermaine Eluemunor: QUESTIONABLE (calf) S Jevón Holland: QUESTIONABLE (concussuon) OL Marcus Mbow: QUESTIONABLE (knee) S Tyler Nubin: QUESTIONABLE (neck) Two names have already been ruled out: Tremaine Edmunds and Greg Newsome, two key pieces of the Giants' defense that have started every game so far this season, yet will miss their first games of the year this weekend in Houston. A couple of other starters for the Giants also appear to be in question leading up to gametime: that's starting right tackle Jermaine Eluemenor and safety Jevon Hollard; both of which would be a major hit to New York's plan of attack on each side of the ball if ruled out. away.headline: Giants Injury Report: Giants O-line Thinned By Injuries
away.blurb: Thomas, who has sat out Wednesday and Thursday over the past several weeks and returned to practice on a limited basis on Friday and Saturday before being cleared to play, is someone to watch this week. Last week he came out of the game just before the big fourth-quarter comeback attempt against the Saints; the veteran left tackle was visibly laboring through his groin injury throughout the game. Starting safety Jevon Holland was spotted at practice, off to the side with a trainer. Newsome and Holland have been the Giants defensive secondary’s best players so far this season, so hopefully their absences aren’t serious enough to keep them out of Sunday’s game. Speaking of the cornerback position, Newsome did not practice, but rookie Colton Hood (concussion) did. Sills, 6-foot-6 and 325 pounds, was originally an undrafted free agent out of Oklahoma State whom the Eagles signed in 2022. That season, Sills, who has played guard in his short NFL career, was one of three undrafted free agents to make the Eagles roster but only appeared in one game for Philadelphia. Giants Injury Report: Giants O-line Thinned By Injuries Skip to main content SI.COM The New York Giants will face one of the best defenses on Sunday when they travel to Houston to meet the Texans. So it was a bit alarming that on Wednesday, the team’s top three offensive tackles were not practicing. Starters Andrew Thomas (groin), Jermaine Eluemunor (calf), and swing tackle Marcus Mbow (knee) were not participating in practice during the media viewing period. Eluemunor missed last week’s game as well with his injury after saying he would test it to see if he could anchor; he is also someone to watch this week. And with MBow now nursing something, the Giants could be thin at offensive tackle if he can’t play. The Texans have league sack leader Will Anderson, Jr. on one side of their formation and Danielle Hunter on the other. That would be quite the test for rookie J.C. Davis, who would presumably play left tackle; at right tackle, the Giants could potentially move Sisi Mauigoa from right guard to tackle, the position he played in college. Edmunds, Newsome Not Spotted During Media Viewing Portion of Practice Inside linebacker Tremaine Edmunds (shoulder) and cornerback Greg Newsome II (concussion) were not spotted at practice during the media viewing portion. If Edmunds can’t go, Micah McFadden would get the start. The question then becomes who would wear the radio in his helmet: rookie Arvell Reese, the most likely candidate, or someone else. Rookie Colton Hood (concussion), receiver Darnell Mooney (neck), safety Tyler Nubin (neck), and tight end Theo Johnson (neck) were spotted at practice during the media viewing portion. Paulson Adebo’s Practice Window Opens Cornerback Paulson Adebo’s 21-day practice window is now open. If he clears, he could fill the roster vacancy left after Tuesday’s release of running back Najee Harris and defensive lineman Jihad Ward. Adebo has been on IR since Week 2

home.headline: Texans will be without star RB for Giants game
home.blurb: David Montgomery out for Texans vs. Giants Pitre previously sat out Week 6, while Blankenship sustained a concussion during the team’s London game. Additionally, offensive tackle Blake Fisher is not expected to play as he nurses a thumb injury while wearing a cast. The Houston Texans beat the Jacksonville Jaguars 34-31 in London last week, with kicker Ka’imi Fairbairn converting both field-goal tries and all four extra points. They brought a long injury list home with them. Houston now turns its attention to the New York Giants. Several Texans stayed off the practice field Thursday, and the absences touched the backfield, the secondary and the offensive line. The Giants have their own concerns, with three offensive tackles missing Wednesday’s session. Houston has one more practice Friday to change any statuses. KPRC 2 Houston’s Aaron Wilson reported what Thursday’s report means for Sunday. MORE: Bold predictions in NFL Week 7: Jahmyr Gibbs, Ja’Marr Chase & more Houston Texans running back David Montgomery will miss Sunday’s game against the New York Giants due to a groin injury (h/t Aaron Wilson of KPRC2). Montgomery is set to miss his second consecutive game after exiting early during the Week 5 victory over the Tennessee Titans. He will not be the only player sidelined for the matchup. The Texans are also expected to be without nickel Jalen Pitre and safety Reed Blankenship, both of whom missed practice alongside Montgomery. MORE: 4 best Jonathan Taylor landing spots at NFL trade deadline How the Texans plan to replace Montgomery against the Giants Woody Marks is in line to lead the backfield again after gaining 56 yards on 15 carries and 25 yards on two catches against the Jaguars. Jawhar Jordan, elevated from the practice squad, added 43 rushing yards and a touchdown on six carries. Wide receiver Tank Dell is on track to make his season debut after returning from injured reserve, head coach DeMeco Ryans said Monday, per Wilson. Dell has not played since tearing multiple knee ligaments in December 2024. Tackle Trent Brown was a full participant Thursday, and tight end Dalton Schultz returned to practice. Those returns help along the offensive line and at tight end as Houston hosts the Giants on Sunday.

home.headline: Texans Injury Report vs. Giants: 3 Starters Ruled Out, Tank Dell Update
home.blurb: And for both sides, it seems like there's due to be some key absences to take note of. In the case of the Texans specifically, there appears to be three starters that will be missing out of the action this Sunday. RB David Montgomery: OUT (groin) S Reed Blankenship: OUT (concussion/hand) WR Tank Dell: QUESTIONABLE (knee) As for those who will be out for their second-straight game, that's none other than versatile defensive back Jalen Pitre, as well as veteran running back David Montgomery . Each will be out of the mix with their respective injuries––albeit minor ones––and will have their next chance to return to the lineup after the bye in Week 9. But the Texans will also be dealing with a couple of new injuries. Starting safety Reed Blankenship will be out for this one as he's still in concussion protocol, but also suffering from a hand issue that will keep him on the sidelines as well. Blankenship left the Texans' last game against the Jaguars in the middle of the first half due to injury, and would inevitably not return to the action. Now for Week 7, that absence within Houston's secondary will continue, and thus leave M.J. Stewart as the most likely fill-in at strong safety next to Calen Bullock. Along with Blankenship, the Texans are also dealing with a new absence to backup offensive tackle Blake Fisher, who's suffering from a thumb injury that doesn't seem to be a serious one given that he hasn't been placed on injured reserve, though will keep him out for this Sunday against New York. While not a starting piece of Houston's offensive front, this offense does like to roll out Fisher as a part of their jumbo packages on that side of the ball, as he's been on the field for over 60 snaps through the first five weeks. One piece of good news for the Texans, however, is the fact that wide receiver Tank Dell has officially been upgraded to questionable. LB Tremaine Edmunds: OUT (shoulder) CB Greg Newsome II: OUT (concussion) TE Theo Johnson: DOUBTFUL (neck) CB Paulson Adebo: QUESTIONABLE (knee) RT Jermaine Eluemunor: QUESTIONABLE (calf) S Jevón Holland: QUESTIONABLE (concussuon) OL Marcus Mbow: QUESTIONABLE (knee) S Tyler Nubin: QUESTIONABLE (neck) Two names have already been ruled out: Tremaine Edmunds and Greg Newsome, two key pieces of the Giants' defense that have started every game so far this season, yet will miss their first games of the year this weekend in Houston. A couple of other starters for the Giants also appear to be in question leading up to gametime: that's starting right tackle Jermaine Eluemenor and safety Jevon Hollard; both of which would be a major hit to New York's plan of attack on each side of the ball if ruled out. He admitted that "without a doubt" it isn't easy to no longer have a starting role. "Whenever you're used to something, you've had a taste of the pie, I guess, and then you don't get to go out there and eat with your boys anymore, it's tough, but I think it's just about staying present," McFadden said. The Giants designated cornerback Paulson Adebo to return this week, and it looks like he could be activated before Sunday's game. With starting cornerback Greg Newsome II still in concussion protocol and ruled out, there could be immediate snaps for Adebo vs. the Texans. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights The Cardinals produce another improbable victory behind a barrage of field goals, and the Dolphins finally hold their first lead of the season Getty Images Anything can happen in the National Football League and the kickoff to Week 7 of the 2026 season certainly solidified that idea. In the Chicago Bears 30-24 win over the New England Patriots , they triumphed despite allowing one of the most unique "Hail Mary" touchdown passes in recent memory. Patriots quarterback Drake Maye's 48-yard checkdown touchdown pass to running back Rhamondre Stevenson was the only touchdown pass in the last 20 years in the final 10 seconds of a half, 40-plus yards from the end zone on a throw of 10 or fewer air yards, per CBS Sports Research. What other craziness could happen during the rest of the NFL's Week 7 lineup? Daniel Jones cuts through Brian Flores' No. 1 Vikings defense The Minnesota Vikings are 5-0, and it is very much on the strength of defensive coordinator Brian Flores' aggressive unit. They are an immovable object. Flores' defense leads the NFL in: Scoring defense (12.8 points per game allowed) Third down defense (22.2% third down conversion rate allowed) Red zone defense (27.3% red zone touchdown rate allowed) Goal-to-go defense (33.3% goal-to-go touchdown rate allowed) Completion percentage allowed (53.2%) Touchdown-to-interception ratio allowed (3-6) Sack rate (9.8%) Pressure rate (46.4%) Blitz rate (69.8%) The Vikings' blitz rate of just under 70% (69.8%) is the highest by any team in any five-game span in the last 10 seasons, per CBS Sports Research. So how is that going to go for Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones in Week 7? Well, the bold prediction here is that he doesn't commit any turnovers and totals multiple touchdowns against Flores' unit. Jones' splits versus the blitz are the exact same in terms of yards per pass attempt this season (5.9), and he actually has a higher completion percentage, touchdown-to-interception ratio, and passer rating against the blitz in 2026. Jones also got to spend the second half of the 2024 season watching how Flores' unit operates up close in practice on a daily basis after Minnesota scooped him up for depth purposes after his New York Giants release. That practice experience against Flores will allow Jones to produce a clean, efficient performance. Daniel Jones vs. the blitz, 2026 season Pass attempts Completion percentage Pass yards per attempt Air yards per attempt Passer rating Bijan Robinson goes runs wild vs. the undefeated 49ers The undefeated San Francisco 49ers not only have a top-five scoring offense (29.5 points per game) but also a top-10 scoring defense (18.3 points allowed per game). That also extends to their run defense, which ranks as the seventh-best in football, allowing just 90.2 rushing yards per game. Bijan Robinson , who enters Week 7 leading the NFL with 785 yards from scrimmage, will go off for 150-plus rushing yards against San Francisco. He'll be well rested after having just 11 touches in Week 6, his fewest in a game since 2024, and Robinson will break what has been one of the 49ers' biggest strengths: their control of outside-zone runs. San Francisco has curbed outside-zone runs to just 3.2 yards per carry, the sixth-fewest in the NFL, and they are the only defense that hasn't allowed a gain of 10 or more yards on those runs, per the NFL's Next Gen Stats. They have also tackled rushers for a loss or no gain on 5 of 29 outside-zone carries, 17.2%. Robinson has 10 explosive runs (gains of 10 or more yards) on his 65 outside-zone carries, tied with Derrick Henry for the most in the league. He's also only been stuffed for no gain or a loss on 6 of his 65 outside-zone run carries. Robinson will repeatedly cook the 49ers, rushing to the outside, and he'll become not only the first player with over 100 yards rushing against San Francisco in 2026 but the first player to hit at least 150 yards rushing against San Francisco. Cardinals stun Broncos without scoring a touchdown The Arizona Cardinals (2-4) upset the preseason Super Bowl favorite Los Angeles Rams 18-16 in Week 6 as 13.5-point road underdogs, earning the second-largest upset win by any team in the last five seasons, according to CBS Sports Research. They accomplished that feat despite not finding the end zone one time. Arizona's 18 points came from six made field goals. The Cardinals host the Denver Broncos (4-2) while seeking their first win away from SoFi Stadium -- both of Arizona's wins have come on the road against the Rams and the Los Angeles Chargers . Denver enters Week 7 with a top 10 scoring defense (20.8 points per game, 10th in the NFL), but Arizona will upset them too for their first home win of the season. Even more impressively, the Cardinals will also beat the Broncos without scoring a touchdown, just like they did with the Rams in Week 6. How will that work? Arizona will pull off that near-impossibility thanks to the Broncos' offensive ceiling being capped by starting quarterback Bo Nix . Nix's 5.6 yards per pass attempt are the fewest in the NFL among quarterbacks to start every game in 2026, and his 4.9 air yards per pass attempt represent the shortest average pass length through six games in the last 20 seasons, according to CBS Sports Research. Not having to defend the deep ball will allow the Cardinals to get creatively aggressive on defense, and Nix will give Arizona's similarly shaky offense, led by journeyman Jacoby Brissett, enough latitude to win with six or seven made field goals and no touchdowns. J.J. McCarthy avoids being sacked vs. Will Anderson Jr., Texans The New York Giants have a new starting quarterback for Week 7 at the Houston Texans : Minnesota Vikings' 2024 10th overall pick castoff J.J. McCarthy . He ranked dead last in the NFL in completion percentage (57.6%), touchdown-to-interception ratio (11-12) and passer rating (72.6) among 33 qualified quarterbacks in 2025. He also had a 10% sack rate last season, the third highest in the entire league. However, McCarthy will not be sacked in his debut as the Giants' starting quarterback despite facing the Houston Texans and All-Pro edge rusher Will Anderson Jr. , the NFL's sacks leader with 7.5 entering Week 7. How will that happen? Perhaps McCarthy has taken a big leap from 2025 to 2026. After checking in for a benched Jameis Winston in the fourth quarter in Week 6, McCarthy threw for 243 yards, the most by any quarterback in the play-by-play era (since 1991) who had no passing yards in the first three quarters, per CBS Sports Research. The humbling he took, being traded for a 2027 fifth-round pick, plus playing in a more simplistic offense in New York under offensive coordinator Matt Nagy and senior offensive assistant Greg Roman, will allow McCarthy to play a cleaner game in Week 7. That will help him avoid Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter's clutches as he avoids being sacked all game long. Dolphins take a lead for the first time this season The Miami Dolphins ' 2026 season is going exactly as one would expect for a franchise paying more for players not on its roster (an NFL-record $179 million in dead cap hits) than for the players on its roster ($156 million). They're 0-5 and have the NFL's worst scoring offense, averaging 14 points per game. They're also just the second team in the Super Bowl era (since 1966) to not have a lead in the first five games of a season, along with the 2005 Houston Texans, per CBS Sports Research. However, they will acquire their first lead in a game of the 2026 season against the New York Jets . The Jets have the worst red zone offense (37.5%) in the NFL, and they haven't scored a touchdown on their last seven red zone trips, which spans the last three games. New York has also been outscored 100-6 in the final two minutes of the first half under Aaron Glenn. Miami will capitalize on Glenn's end-of-the-first-half mismanagement and take a lead in a game for the first time this season. Next on the docket is a scrappy Arizona Cardinals bunch that just pulled a huge road upset of the Los Angeles Rams. The good news for the Broncos (4-2) is that they got the mini-bye week before heading to the desert and could get a few players back from injury and the commissioner's exempt list. Denver looks to extend its winning streak to three games after coming out of a gauntlet to start the season. The Broncos are currently -4.5-point road favorites over Arizona (2-4). The total sits at over/under 43.5 points, with a lean toward the over at -115. Offensive Rankings Denver : Thirty-first in total offense (252.2 yards per game), 26th in rushing offense (84.2 YPG), 28th in passing offense (168.0 YPG), 26th in scoring offense (19.0 points per game). Arizona : Twenty-third in total offense (307.3 yards per game), 22nd in rushing offense (96.3 YPG), 20th in passing offense (211.0 YPG), 24th in scoring offense (21.0 points per game). Defensive Rankings Denver : Twenty-second in total defense (348.3 yards per game), 31st in rushing defense (139.8 YPG), 10th in passing defense (208.5 YPG), tied for 10th in scoring defense (20.8 points per game). Arizona : Twenty-third in total defense (350.5 yards per game), 20th in rushing defense (120.8 YPG), 22nd in passing defense (229.7 YPG), tied for 31st in scoring defense (29.7 points per game). Here are the MHR staff's keys to Sunday's game. Win the line of scrimmage on offense The Broncos offensive line has been the definition of "meh" to start the regular season. It's nowhere near what it's been the last few seasons, but it also isn't horrid either. Denver needs to dominate the line of scrimmage on Sunday. Open lanes in the running game and do a better job of pass protection. It's a cliche, but success on offense starts in the trenches. Getting that could lay the foundation for jump-starting the offense. — Ian St. Clair Bench Bo Nix; Start Jarrett Stidham Just kidding. Ya'll crazy if you think benching Bo Nix is even remotely the answer. That said, Bo Nix does need to play better, and he isn't seeing the field well to start the season. He's had slow starts in every season he's played, so, for now, I'm chalking this up to another slow start. However, seven games in, I'm hoping to see him take flight a bit now that the hardest part of the Broncos' schedule is complete. At 4-2, they got through it with a winning record, and that is all we could hope for. — Tim Lynch Pressure the QB The key to this game is the same as it has been every week. Get to the QB. The defense has done a great job this season of causing mayhem in the backfield. Make it uncomfortable for Jacoby Brissett (like the back of a Volkswagen). When QBs are harassed and hurried, they make mistakes. — Adam Malnati Disciplined, execution-based offensive football This team needs to execute at a high level, and it will win this game easily. The defense is already there. If the offense can up its game, this Broncos team will be unstoppable. — Sadaraine Limit the impact of Trey McBride The Broncos defense has performed well this season, aside from a few games. For the most part, they've been able to limit the impact of the opposing team's top player on their offense. This week, they face All-Pro tight end Trey McBride, who is coming off a sensational 2025 season. He is the focal point of Arizona's aerial attack and gets over ten targets per game. Defensive coordinator Vance Joseph needs to come up with a good game plan that limits his impact on the game. If they can slow him down, Denver will have a great shot at earning their fifth victory of the season. — Christopher Hart What are your keys to Sunday's game?

picks.headline: 4 bold predictions in the Arizona Cardinals' matchup vs. the Broncos on Larry Fitzgerald's day
picks.blurb: Larry Fitzgerald goes into the Ring of Honor at halftime Sunday, and the Arizona Cardinals will retire his No. 11 in front of a crowd that hasn’t seen a home win this season. Arizona is 0-2 at State Farm Stadium, outscored 76-28, and the Denver Broncos arrive for a 1:05 p.m. kickoff in the Valley. The mood is better than the record. Arizona (2-4) beat the Rams 18-16 as a 12.5-point underdog on six Chad Ryland field goals, and Nick Rallis found the defense the Cardinals needed. They’re 4.5-point underdogs again, and here are four calls for a Fitzgerald-sized afternoon. Trey McBride catches 10 passes Trey McBride’s 49 catches are tied for the NFL lead, and he played 70 of 72 snaps against the Rams. He’s the first thing that should scare the Broncos , and Mike LaFleur wants his receivers to dream of man coverage when defenses double him. Denver might not have the people to cover him. Pat Surtain II has missed two games with an ankle injury and was limited all week, and safety Talanoa Hufanga hasn’t practiced. Jahdae Barron allowed nine catches on 12 targets against Seattle, and his 41.6 coverage grade has the Broncos thinking about a trade. McBride gets 10 catches and passes 100 yards. Arizona scores two red zone touchdowns Arizona went 0 for 5 in the red zone in Los Angeles and still won, the franchise’s first road win without a touchdown since 2014, according to Next Gen Stats. The Cardinals score touchdowns on 47.8% of red zone trips, 27th in the league. They know it can’t continue. “We can’t kick six field goals and expect to win football games,” LaFleur told the team’s website . McBride said it more simply: “We have to score touchdowns in this league.” Denver allows 44.4% of third downs to be converted, 25th in the NFL, and that gives Jacoby Brissett enough chances to finish two drives in the end zone. Josh Sweat sacks Bo Nix twice Josh Sweat had a team-high four pressures and a sack on 25 pass-rush snaps against the Rams, and the noise around him as a trade target hasn’t quieted. He has two sacks and 10 pressures this season, per PFF . “People think I forgot how to play football,” Sweat said after the win . Bo Nix has 230 passing yards in his past two games and averages 4.9 air yards per attempt, the lowest through six games in 20 years. Denver hasn’t been pushing the ball downfield, and Rallis called a season-high 13 blitzes against the Rams. Budda Baker, who has 3.5 sacks, didn’t practice Wednesday or Thursday, but Sweat doesn’t need him. He gets Nix twice. The Cardinals win on Fitzgerald’s day Denver leads the all-time series 10-1-1, and its 14 straight one-score regular-season wins say it knows how to close. Its offense ranks 31st in yards, though, and has scored 40 points in the two games since Sean Payton took over play-calling. Zach Allen, a Cardinal from 2019 to 2022, leads all interior defenders with 26 pressures, per PFF , so Brissett will have to get rid of the ball quickly. This one comes down to a kick, and Ryland is 14 of 16 and on pace to top Neil Rackers’ franchise scoring record . Arizona wins 20-17, and the NFC West conversation gets a little louder at 3-4.

away.headline: Broncos Week 7 Injury Report: Final Decisions on Surtain, Coleman & Hufanga
away.blurb: Given the gauntlet of opponents the Broncos faced to get to 4-2, they earned those three days. The question is whether that chance to breathe gave Sean Payton enough time to tweak the Broncos' offense, dig Bo Nix out of his slump, and get the run game firing on all cylinders. The Broncos are starting to get healthier. That may be a relative term, given that three players have been ruled out, but it's more about the caliber of players returning. Surtain is questionable after returning to practice on Wednesday . He was limited all three days this week, so if he's fully healthy, he'll play. If not, the Broncos will be wise and wait until Week 8 to insert him back into the lineup. Coleman is also listed as questionable, but only because Sean Payton wants Arizona to wonder for as long as possible whether the Broncos will actually activate their rookie running back. The Broncos started Coleman's clock to return from injured reserve earlier this week. It's great to see Moss back to full participation. And Waddle has been fully cleared, though he was limited the first two days of the week. Badie, Elliss, and Hufanga are out this week. It wouldn't be a surprise to see Badie and Elliss placed on IR to make room for Coleman and the return of veteran rush linebacker Jonathon Cooper, who's expected to come back from the commissioner's exempt list this week. Budda Baker is slow to get up. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Out We'll be closely monitoring Baker's status on gameday. He did not practice on Wednesday or Thursday, and was limited on Friday, but it'll be a surprise if he doesn't suit up. Denver's actual bye isn't until Week 10. This matchup with the Cardinals could answer that question and more, given that they rank bottom 10 in net yards and points allowed. It's a road game, and the Cardinals are coming off a big win over the Los Angeles Rams, but if Nix and Payton's offense can't get right against the NFL's second-worst scoring defense, it will only deepen doubts that the Broncos will ever turn the ship around this season. Coleman is officially listed as questionable. Elsewhere on the injury front, cornerback Pat Surtain ( ankle ) is listed as questionable while wide receiver Jaylen Waddle ( chest ) and cornerback Riley Moss ( ribs ) have been cleared to play. away.headline: Pat Surtain injury: Latest updates for Broncos cornerback
away.blurb: Denver Broncos cornerback Pat Surtain went down with a non-contact ankle injury late in the second quarter of Sunday's game against the San Francisco 49ers . He was ruled out in the third quarter. Broncos CB Pat Surtain questionable for Week 7 Denver's injury report for Sunday's game against Arizona has cornerback Pat Surtain officially listed as questionable . If he can't play, Jahdae Barron will likely be the next man up. Despite returning to practice on Wednesday, Pat Surtain seems more likely to return in Week 8 against the Chiefs, according to James Palmer of NFL on Prime Video . We'll see how the week goes for PS2. Pat Surtain might not return in Week 7 In an updated report on Pat Surtain's status, James Palmer of Prime Video clarified that PS2's injury was not a non-contact injury — it actually happened one play before the cornerback went down on the field. Palmer also reported that " [i]t might be tough " for Surtain to return to action in Week 7, suggesting PS2 might be more likely to return in Week 8. Pat Surtain ruled out for Week 6; there's hope for possible Week 7 return Pat Surtain has been ruled out for a Thursday Night Football clash with the Seattle Seahawks in Week 6, but there is hope he might be able to return against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 7, according to KUSA-TV's Mike Klis . Pat Surtain avoids IR; ruled out for Week 5 ESPN's Adam Schefter said on Altitude Sports Radio that his guess is that Pat Surtain will land on injured reserve , which would rule the cornerback out for at least four games. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported this morning that Pat Surtain is expected to miss time, but it's not believed to be season-ending. "You hope it is just a couple weeks, maybe it ends up in an IR stint, but not expected to be season-ending," Rapoport said . If Surtain is placed on injured reserve, he would have to sit out at least four games. Broncos CB Pat Surtain ruled out Broncos cornerbacks Pat Surtain (ankle) and Riley Moss (ribs), who were both originally listed as questionable to return, have been announced as ruled out for the rest of today's game. Riley Moss and Jahdae Barron are the two outside cornerbacks with Ja'Quan McMillian playing in the slot. Behind them on Denver's depth chart , the Broncos also have Kris Abrams-Draine. With PS2 sidelined, the team is down to four healthy cornerbacks on the active roster. Update : Moss (ribs) was announced as questionable to return after halftime, so Denver now has Barron and Abrams-Draine starting at the two outside cornerback spots. Surtain was down on the field for a few moments before being helped off by two people, walking slowly into the locker room. Surtain was replaced on defense by cornerback Jahdae Barron, the team's first-round pick in last year's NFL draft. Barron played across from Riley Moss with Ja'Quan McMillian continuing to play in the slot. Surtain had totaled four tackles in the first half before leaving the game. away.headline: Latest Broncos' injury report indicates key players are nearing a return
away.blurb: Running back Jonah Coleman, who has been designated to return from IR with his ankle injury, practiced in full on Wednesday. Patrick Surtain II, who left the team's Week 4 game with an ankle injury, was also at practice on a limited basis: Unfortunately, Tyler Badie, Talanoa Hufanga, and Jonah Elliss all did not practice, and Elliss' injury could end up being more extended. Hufanga hurt his ankle in Week 5 against the Los Angeles Chargers, and both Badie and Elliss got hurt in Week 6 against the Seattle Seahawks. Fortunately, Hufanga's injury is minor. As for Surtain, James Palmer is reporting that the likely return for the Defensive Player of the Year is Week 8 against Kansas City, but he also didn't totally shut the door on Surtain playing this week : Him practicing in limited fashion does give him a chance to play, but you almost want to wonder if the Broncos understand the opponents they have coming up and want to ease Surtain back into things for Week 8, as that game could carry major impact across the division and conference in terms of seeding. All in all, the Broncos seem to be trending toward being more 'full strength' for the Chiefs game in Week 8. However, not only could Coleman find his way back into the lineup in Week 7, but, until he's ruled out, Surtain could be nearing a return as well. The Broncos also have wide receiver Pat Bryant on IR. He is eligible to return f in Week 9 against the Carolina Panthers. Denver plays Arizona, Kansas City, and Carolina before the Week 10 bye, which just so happens to line up nicely with the trade deadline. This article was originally published on predominantlyorange.com as Latest Broncos' injury report indicates key players are nearing a return . The Denver Broncos have dealt with their share of injuries this year, unfortunately. The bright side though, is that the Broncos are consistently among the least-injured teams in the NFL, and the ailments this year have largely been minor. As the middle of the season approaches, the playoff race will slowly start to heat up, and Week 8 against the Kansas City Chiefs could present a legitimate playoff atmosphere. Before the Chiefs, though, the Broncos have to get by the Arizona Cardinals in Week 7. And in the team's first injury report of the week, it does seem to indicate that the team could get some key players back. away.source: Denver Broncos On SI on MSN
away.blurb: Coleman was designated to return from injured reserve on Wednesday after missing the last four games. He still must be formally activated to the 53-man roster but is fully expected to play against the Cardinals. Coleman's return is especially helpful this week considering third-string RB Tyler Badie missed practice for a second straight day due to a thumb injury. His status for Sunday's game is in jeopardy; he needs a limited session Friday to have any chance of suiting up. Outside linebacker Jonah Elliss (ankle) and safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) both also were DNPs this week. Hufanga will be ruled out on Friday, and the Broncos anticipate Elliss landing on short-term injured reserve, back at some point later this year. “He’s going to be someone that it’s not season-ending, and so we’re fortunate. So that’ll come out later in the week, but it was better news," head coach Sean Payton said of Elliss on Wednesday. Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest) and cornerback Patrick Surtain II (ankle) were limited participants; Surtain could be a game-time decision, though Waddle is expected to go. Arizona listed starting safety Budda Baker and running back Jeremiyah Love as DNP for a second consecutive day, as well as safety Andrew Wingard. Cornerback Garrett Williams and defensive lineman Darius Robinson were upgraded to limited. “They give you a couple different looks," Payton noted Wednesday. "They’re in their base defense. They have a penny package. You have to I.D. if they’re in that. Then their pressure package from nickel. They affect the quarterback. I think the other thing that stands out is they’re causing more fumbles in their wins. Their takeaway numbers have been really good, and that’s something you see.” Broncos Get Massive Boost with Return of RB Jonah Coleman Broncos' IR Watch: Who's Eligible to Return and What They Bring The Denver Broncos continued full-scale preparation for Sunday's road game against the Arizona Cardinals, releasing their second injury report ahead of the Week 7 matchup. On it, running back Jonah Coleman (ankle) and cornerback Riley Moss (ribs) were listed as full practice participants for another day, while defensive end Zach Allen was upgraded to full after getting his usual rest day on Wednesday. Cardinals Might Be Down Some Starpower Unfortunately for the home team, the Cardinals are trending toward being at much less than full strength -- at least, according to their Thursday injury report . Baker's absence in particular would be a fortuitous break for a Broncos offense desperately seekin its first true breakout game in 2026. However, Payton knows well enough not to overlook the other 10 players on the Cardinals' defensive side. home.blurb: Head coach Mike LaFleur announced the news in his press conference on Friday, Oct. 23, ahead of the Cardinals' game against the Denver Broncos. This marks the second consecutive game that Love has missed as the Cardinals, following a nagging ankle injury that limited his explosiveness in recent weeks. In addition to Love, LaFleur ruled out defensive tackle Walter Nolen, safety Andrew Wingard and right guard Jon Gaines. Nolen, the Cardinals’ 2025 first-round pick, injured his ankle in the third quarter of last week’s win over the Rams . He returned to the game but came up limping after a snap late in the fourth quarter and did not return. Gaines is the newest addition to the injury report, as he suffered an ankle injury in practice on Thursday, Oct. 22. “Enough to keep him out for this week,” LaFleur said. The same goes for defensive lineman Darius Robinson, who was downgraded to questionable with a back injury on Thursday. LaFleur said that the situation is “similar” with cornerback Max Melton, who was limited on Wednesday and did not practice on Thursday due to a knee injury. When asked, LaFleur said the Cardinals have not discussed placing Love on injured reserve. In Love's absence, the Cardinals will once again turn to Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight to lead their backfield. In Week 6, Allgeier finished with 18 carries for 38 yards, while Knight took 15 carries for 80 yards. Both players saw two targets, while Allgeier led in snap share, 56% to 44%. LaFleur described Allgeier as more of the Cardinals’ third-down back, whereas Knight’s role is more on first and second downs. Last week, Allgeier played on 10 of 15 third downs. On first and second down, Allgeier had 29 snaps to Knight’s 26. “(Allgeier) is extremely smart, so he's very beneficial for us on third downs, with the protection schemes, with his firmness, in terms of picking up pressures,” LaFleur said. “… So he provides that skill set for us. He can still do what we need on first and second down, but that's where Bam ends up coming in and doing a lot of that work on first and second down.” LaFleur said that the Cardinals do not expect Nolen to be placed on injured reserve, but he left the door more open there than he did with Love. “Don't expect, but as I've learned through seven weeks of the job, I expect anything,” LaFleur said. “But I just answer it with him; he's no different than all the other guys. Not expecting it, but there are setbacks. These are human bodies.” Wingard, meanwhile, will miss his third consecutive game after suffering a knee injury against the Giants in Week 4. The Cardinals have multiple options to fill his void at safety, with Wydett Williams and Dadrion Taylor-Demerson both now healthy. They could also play cornerback Garrett Williams in that spot, as they did last week. The Cardinals will turn to 2025 sixth-round pick Hayden Conner in Gaines’ absence. home.headline: Denver Broncos Make Patrick Surtain II Announcement Before Cardinals Game
home.blurb: The Denver Broncos announced a significant injury update on cornerback Patrick Surtain II on Friday, October 23, leaving the door open for their defensive superstar to return against the Arizona Cardinals. Surtain has been listed as questionable for Sunday's Week 7 matchup as he continues recovering from an ankle injury that has sidelined him for the past two games. The designation comes after Surtain participated in all three practices this week, although he remained limited throughout. It marks his first week of practice participation since suffering the injury against the San Francisco 49ers on October 4. Patrick Surtain II Could Return After Missing Two Broncos Games Surtain suffered a non-contact ankle injury during Denver's Week 4 loss to San Francisco and did not return to the contest. That changed Wednesday, when Surtain returned to the practice field. He subsequently logged three consecutive limited sessions before receiving his questionable designation Friday. Hufanga was ruled out Friday with an ankle injury after missing all three practices this week. The Broncos also ruled out outside linebacker Jonah Elliss and running back Tyler Badie. His questionable designation means his availability remains uncertain, and his status will become official when the Broncos announce their game-day inactives approximately 90 minutes before kickoff. The Broncos also listed rookie running back Jonah Coleman as questionable. Coleman practiced fully all three days after being designated to return from injured reserve, but he must be activated before he can play. Still, the injury forced Surtain to miss Denver's victories over the Los Angeles Chargers and Seattle Seahawks. He did not participate in practice ahead of either game. The Broncos now face a decision about whether to bring their All-Pro cornerback back against Arizona or give him additional recovery time. Most recently, the Matt LaFleur-led squad dispatched of the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football, 23-13. It marked the third consecutive game in which Green Bay held its opponent to 14 or fewer points. And on the season, the Packers’ defense – coordinated by former Arizona Cardinals head coach Jonathan Gannon – has allowed the 10th-fewest points in the NFL (20.8/game). Meanwhile, on the opposite side of the ball, Green Bay – led under center by sixth-year passer Jordan Love – has scored the 10th-fewest points in the game (21.2/game). Through six weeks, Love has also completed just 59.7 percent of his pass attempts. If the season ended today, it'd rank as his lowest completion percentage as a starting quarterback in the NFL. Yet, multiple Green Bay pass-catchers have flourished, most notably wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. Watson, now in his fifth NFL season, has already amassed as many touchdowns as last season (six) and nearly as many receptions (29) and reception yards as he did a year ago (538). The former second-round pick secured 35 catches and 611 yards in 10 games a season ago. Meanwhile, Golden, Green Bay's first-round pick in 2025, has already surpassed all his receiving totals from his rookie campaign. He's already racked up 30 catches, 501 yards and three touchdowns amid a career breakout season. And just like Watson, he's well on pace for a 1,000-yard receiving campaign. Consequently, both Watson and Golden possess the potential to wreak havoc against the Lions’ secondary, even with Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch back in the fold for Detroit. In addition to Watson and Golden, the Lions will also likely have their hands full with Packers running back Josh Jacobs. The Pro Bowler returns to the lineup after spending the first six weeks of the season on the commissioner exempt list for an offseason domestic abuse incident. Jacobs, who's coming off a 929-yard, 13-touchdown rushing campaign in 2025, should provide an immediate boost to Green Bay's league-worst ground game. In case you were wondering, the Packers have compiled a measly 359 total rushing yards through the season's first six games. Expect Jacobs, along with Watson and Golden, to give Kelvin Sheppard's defense its fair share of fits on Sunday. However, at this present juncture, I'm still willing to give the Lions a 60 percent chance to pull off the Week 7 victory at home.
