Last week, the team's matchup with the Dallas Cowboys at Lambeau Field stayed well under the total, thanks in large part to an excellent effort by Jonathan Gannon's defense. This week, however, could be a very different story. On Sunday afternoon, the Packers play the Detroit Lions at Ford Field, a venue that has been the site of several high-scoring games between these two teams in recent years. FanDuel Sportsbook has the total points line set at 52.5 once again, the highest line for a game between these two teams since 2020, when it was set at a whopping 55.5. It's just what these teams do — well, except for in 2022, a game that was a bizarre defensive slugfest. But look at those results starting in 2023, when Jordan Love took over at quarterback — the Packers haven't scored fewer than 29 points at Ford Field with him behind center. Who will win the game? That's less certain, as the results above show, with the two teams each taking three of the last six games at Ford Field. APC is a bit split on this one, as you'll see in our picks below. But one thing we're not split on is taking the over. Given the Packers' issues defending against an elite running back earlier this year — and considering Jahmyr Gibbs is certainly in the Bijan Robinson echelon — plus the Lions' abysmal passing defense, this game should shape up to be a wild one. LeBron's biggest comeback High Stakes in Motown: Three Bold Predictions for Lions vs. Packers (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect) Dakota Allen Fri, October 23, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The classic NFC North rivalry reignites this Sunday at Ford Field in a clash carrying massive divisional implications. The Detroit Lions return home fresh off their bye week seeking to re-establish dominance in the North, while Jordan Love and the red-hot Green Bay Packers roll into town riding high momentum. Extra rest gives Dan Campbell's coaching staff two full weeks to scheme, but Matt LaFleur's offense has been operating with surgical precision. When these two powerhouse rosters collide, subplots will fly. Here are three bold predictions for Sunday's showdown. 1. Jahmyr Gibbs Out-Gains Green Bay's Entire Rushing Attack The Packers have leaned heavily on Jordan Love's arm, but their ground game has yielded inconsistent results throughout the early stretch of the season. Conversely, Detroit's dynamic backfield partner Jahmyr Gibbs comes into this contest thoroughly rested and ready to explode. Drew Petzing will feature Gibbs heavily in both the running and short-passing games to negate Green Bay's aggressive pass rush. Expect Gibbs to turn limited touches into game-breaking plays, accumulating over 130 total scrimmage yards on his own, out-gaining the Packers' team rushing output by the final whistle. 2. Aidan Hutchinson Hits a Career High in Single-Game Pressures Detroit's defensive anchor Aidan Hutchinson has been relentless up front. With the extra rest enabling him to rush at full throttle, Hutchinson faces a Green Bay offensive line that will be forced into passing situations if Detroit grabs an early lead. The prediction: Hutchinson completely disrupts Green Bay's passing rhythm, generating at least eight total quarterback pressures and logging 2.5 sacks on Jordan Love. His motor off the edge will keep Ford Field roaring and force Love into uncomfortable platform throws under pressure. 3. Amon-Ra St. Brown and Xavier McKinney Trade Game-Changing Playmaking This match features a high-stakes duel between elite stars: Detroit's top wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown and Green Bay's ball-hawking safety Xavier McKinney. St. Brown will find his usual rhythm in the slot, hauling in double-digit receptions and at least one touchdown. However, McKinney won't leave Detroit empty-handed. Expect McKinney to jump an intermediate route for a critical second-half interception, setting up a nail-biting, fourth-quarter finish between two teams that refuse to give an inch. Divisional matchups coming off a bye week often turn into instant classics, and this one is going to be nothing short of that. While Green Bay enters Ford Field with plenty of heat, Detroit's fresh legs and hyper-aggressive offensive design should prove just enough to secure a thrilling victory at home. I expect this one to be back and forth until the final whistle.

picks.headline: Lions vs. Packers preview: 3 key matchups
picks.blurb: Lions vs. Packers preview: 3 key matchups - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football World Series preview NFL injury updates Knicks change ring tune Cowboys not trading? LeBron's biggest comeback Lions vs. Packers preview: 3 key matchups Detroit Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard reacts to a play against Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the first half at Ford Field in Detroit on Monday, Oct. 20, 2025. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Anthony Balaj Fri, October 23, 2026 at 10:30 AM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Detroit Lions (3-2) will have an opportunity to reestablish themselves in the NFC North in both Week 7 and Week 8 as the Green Bay Packers (4-2) and the Minnesota Vikings (5-0) travel to Ford Field. This is not a situation most Lions fans are very familiar with. In my lifetime, the storyline with these types of divisional games was whether the Lions could finally establish themselves as true division contenders. But never to reestablish as one. Just take the 2025 NFC North standings in for a moment. Look at them again. I've seen the Lions at the bottom far too often in my 34 years. After getting the taste of what it was like at the top in 2023 and 2024, it felt like last place would never be the case again as long as Dan Campbell was leading the Lions. Unfortunately, it happened. Oh, and look. It could happen again because this division is the best in football. It's not slowing down. The race is on. Brian Flores and the Vikings defense is not waiting for the Lions young offensive line to gel before it comes to Detroit. Ben Johnson and the Chicago Bears are not waiting for the Lions young defensive coordinator to find his footing while seeking to repeat as division champs. Matt LaFleur and the Packers are not waiting to the Lions secondary to solve its problems before attacking it with deep shot after deep shot. No, the Lions are at the bottom. Feel it. Breathe it in. Remember the decades at the bottom. In a way, it feels like this is truly the first game of the season. This is how it was always meant to be. Don't get me wrong, the 2023 and 2024 teams are without question the best and most memorable seasons of my Lions fandom. But the story of Dan Campbell's Detroit Lions was always meant to overcome adversity. To get kicked in the teeth. To get knocked down. But before long, they are going to be the last ones standing. Three key matchups. Three opportunity to reestablish . Ford Field vs. Packers' offense Green Bay comes into Ford Field ranking 29th in presnap penalties with 22 on the season . The key matchup here is the Lions fans at Ford Field against the Packers' discipline before the snap. Of course, presnap penalties are drive killer for most any NFL offense. But that is amplified for the Packers who have no running game and are last last in rushing yards per game (59.8), yards per carry (2.9), and rush EPA (-0.299) . Playing behind the sticks making the Packers even more one-dimensional would be extremely valuable for a Lions' secondary that could use all the help it could get, especially with rookie Keith Abney likely to play often at the safety position. In 2025, the Lions were the beneficiary on only 18 false start penalties, tied for 22nd in the NFL. To go with the 5-3 record on the season, Ford Field was hardly the home field advantage that it had been in the years prior. Sunday is an opportunity to reestablish Ford Field as being one of the most difficult environments for opposing teams to play in. Let me just drop this in here one more time. Kelvin Sheppard vs. poison picked The second key matchup was highlighted well by Jeremy Reisman's question to defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard asking how do does he decide on your poison in a matchup that presents both deep and over-the-middle weapons? "That is the coach's job to make sure that we understand the down and distancing, the tendencies and things like that. What have we seen? And obviously each game things change. You prepare. These coaches are good in this league and they self-scout as well." The Green Bay Packers' deep passing attack is a bit of a paper tiger with some interesting situational tendencies , but nevertheless, it must be respected out of the sheer frequency they attempt it. Last week against the Arizona Cardinals, Sheppard rolled out a unique solution by bracket covering both Trey McBride and Michael Wilson . It won't be that simple this week as the Packers have two deep threats in wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden, as well as tight end Tucker Kraft. With the return of safety Brian Branch, Sheppard has the flexibility to pick his poison by game script, down-and-distance, and personnel groupings to put the defense in the best position for success. Branch's return to the field is an opportunity for the Lions secondary to reestablish itself, and it could not have come at a more critical time. Cade Mays vs. Jonathan Gannon Lastly, the third key matchup is Lions' center Cade Mays vs. Packers' defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon. Mays is set to make his Detroit Lions debut with his first start of the season. Gannon is in his first season as Green Bay's defensive coordinator and so far he has made some significant adjustments to his normal defensive philosophy. As discussed in "The Athletic Football Show" clip below, Gannon is dialing up blitzes of 6+ rushing defenders at 2-3 times the rate as he had in either Arizona or Philadelphia. It will be critical for Mays and Jared Goff to be on the same page regarding blitz recognition and communication. If successful, it is very likely the Lions offense reaches 30+ points scored against. Consider this Mays' introduction by fire to the blitz-heavy NFC North, wherein all three of the Vikings (1st, 66.7%), Bears (5th, 39.6%), and (Packers (10th, 32.1%) are in the top ten in the NFL in blitz rate, according to Sumer Sports . Mays has the opportunity to reestablish the Lions offensive line as one of the most intelligent and powerful units in the NFL since the retirement of Frank Ragnow. These are the matchups. These are the opportunities for the Lions to reestablish as the class of the NFC North once again.

home.blurb: Packers rule out Zaire Franklin, list four questionable vs. Lions | Week 7 Injury Report Skip to main content Primary nav News Evan Siegle, packers.com LB Zaire Franklin GREEN BAY – Packers have officially ruled out linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin) and listed four questionable for Sunday's NFC North matchup with the Detroit Lions. The four questionable are guard Aaron Banks (knee/toe), cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), receiver Bo Melton (back) and defensive tackle Jordon Riley (Achilles), who's currently on the physically unable to perform list and would need to be added to the 53-man roster to play against the Lions. Sunday will mark only the second game Franklin has missed in nine NFL seasons, snapping a streak of 48 consecutive games played dating back to Week 8 of the 2023 season when the former All-Pro linebacker sat out against Carolina with a knee injury. The Packers could have reinforcements on the way up front against the Lions and star running back Jahmyr Gibbs, as Riley appears to be nearing a return. The third-year defensive tackle has practiced in a limited capacity the past two weeks, his first on-field work since tearing his Achilles last December. Banks has been out since injuring his toe against the New York Jets in Week 2. The 6-foot-5, 325-pound guard was also battling knee tendinitis at the time of his toe injury. Veteran Laken Tomlinson has started the past three games at left guard. The Packers didn't issue a game status for the following players who will be available: quarterback Jordan Love (back), edge rusher Lukas Van Ness (illness), cornerback Brandon Cisse (shoulder/neck), defensive tackle Anthony Campbell (ankle), and receivers Christian Watson (ankle), Matthew Golden (shoulder) and Savion Williams (ankle). Lions safety Brian Branch (Achilles) and center Cade Mays (wrist) were full participants in practice this week but are both questionable for Sunday. home.blurb: Defensive captain Zaire Franklin is out with a shin injury, while Edgerrin Cooper is out for the season. Zaire Franklin , a defensive captain, took a knee to his shin in practice Oct. 22 and will not play against the Detroit Lions on Sunday, Oct. 25. The Packers already are without Edgerrin Cooper , who is out for the season after tearing his Achilles a few weeks ago. According to the final injury report, Zaire Franklin (shin) is out. Aaron Banks (knee/toe), Bo Melton (back), Jordon Riley (IR/Achilles) and Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring) are questionable to play. Packers running back Josh Jacobs participated in practice this week, and could be set to return. He’s been out with a back injury. Packers guard Aaron Banks participated in practice all week, making it possible he’s set to return to game action. He also participated in a full week of practice last week, but was ruled out for the Week 6 game against the Dallas Cowboys. He’s been available for only one game this season, the first half of the Week 2 game against the New York Jets. LaFleur said he has been pleased with Riley's progress as he’s working toward his return from injured reserve following last year’s season-ending Achilles injury. Backups Isaiah McDuffie and Ty’Ron Hopper will face Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs. GREEN BAY – In a matchup against one of the NFL’s most-explosive running backs, the Green Bay Packers will be without both of their starting linebackers. That will leave backups Isaiah McDuffie, a special-teams captain, and Ty’Ron Hopper to contain Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs. “I don’t believe it’s going to be anything too long term,” coach Matt LaFleur said when asked if Franklin’s injury might put him on injured reserve. “Just an unfortunate deal. That happens when you play football, especially with the way our guys have been practicing, but I think we’ve got a lot of confidence in McDuffie and Hopper and Nick Niemann, if need be, to go in there and do a great job for us.” Even if Franklin’s injury is short term, the timing isn’t ideal. Gibbs ranks fifth in the NFL with 504 rushing yards and is tied for second in the league with seven rushing touchdowns. A dual-threat, his 27 receptions are third among running backs in the league. He has 243 receiving yards and a pair of touchdown catches. Gibbs is the engine behind a Lions offense tied with the Buffalo Bills in league scoring at 32.8 points per game. McDuffie has started in place of Cooper the past two weeks. Hopper, a third-round draft pick in 2024, has only 78 defensive snaps this season but has shown potential, especially in coverage. He had a goal-line interception two weeks ago against the Chicago Bears and has added a pair of pass breakups. “He’s maximized [his snaps],” LaFleur said. “He’s taken advantage of them. LeBron's biggest comeback Rams vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 7 Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints Thu, October 22, 2026 at 6:41 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads There is a big time injury for the Los Angeles Rams . And the Raiders have a major concern as well. These teams meet in Week 7, and here are bold predictions for the NFL contest. It's a crucial game for the Rams, who stand at 2-4 and find themselves a staggering four games behind the front-running 49ers in the NFC West. Meanwhile, the Raiders stand at 3-3 in third place in the AFC West. They're unlikely to be a playoff contender, but are trying to build a strong foundation for 2027. Let's take a look at what could happen when these teams battle. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Matthew Stafford will throw for three touchdowns It's hard to gauge what kind of yardage output Stafford will have. Without the injured Davante Adams, the Rams may lean on the ground game a little more. Adams is the team's leading receiver with 480 yards and four touchdowns. Sure, Stafford still has Puka Nacua. And Nacua will get his targets and yardage. But who steps into the No. 2 role? Maybe the Rams will use tight end Tyler Higbee more. Or perhaps Konata Mumpfield or Jordan Whittington will step up and produce. However, despite the receiver situation, the Rams will need to find a way to get the ball into the end zone if the Raiders load up to stop the run in the red zone. So look for Stafford to spread it around and still get his TD passes. Stafford said he understands the situation , according to The Athletic. "I just feel even more responsibility to try to be as good as I can be to help us continue to win," Stafford said. "In some of those guys' instances where they're going to have opportunities to hopefully come back and play for us, make sure that when they come back and play for us, it's meaningful stuff for them." However, some observers think Stafford has finally reached the end of his NFL rope, according to ESPN. "Stafford can't move," Ben Solak wrote. "He was never the most mobile quarterback, but the Rams were willing to use him on boots in the past. In 2024, 16.8% of Stafford's pass attempts were on the run — an above-average number! That fell to 13.9% in 2025 and is down to 9.6% in 2026. Sure, designed rollouts are down — but it isn't just that. "Stafford has zero scrambling passing yards on the season per NFL Next Gen Stats. He has yet to break the pocket and complete a pass on a scramble drill. The last quarterback to log no scramble passing yards through six weeks of a season was 2022 Tom Brady — the final season of a pocket passing titan." But it's not time to write Stafford off. Rams RB Kyren Williams will rush for 90-plus yards The Rams must run the football against the Raiders, a team that struggles to stop the ground game. The Raiders are giving up 134.3 yards per game, which ranks No. 28 in the NFL. Keeping the ball on the ground needs to be a big part of the Rams' game plan. The Rams have thrown 252 passes with 148 rushing attempts. McVay wants those numbers closer together , according to theramswire.com. "Ultimately, what I care about and what we care about is what's the best way is to move the ball and score points," McVay said. "Because of some of the situations that we've been in, those two-minute situations have gotten us a little bit out of balance. No matter how I cut it, it's an excuse. I'd like to be able to have a little bit more balance. And that's reflected by being efficient on early downs and sustaining drives." One thing is for sure, Williams and the Rams haven't lost their belief that this can be a special season. "Man, my confidence is still as high as ever," Williams said. "We know what we've got on our team and in this locker room. We come to practice every single week. That's why we can't lose our focus. We can't lose what matters the most, and that's the work. "It's about having faith. That the work we put in every single week will come to shine." Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty will split carries with Mike Washington Jr. There's no doubt that Jeanty has been a huge disappointment for the Raiders. They picked him No. 6 overall, expecting a franchise-changing player. Instead, Jeanty has a career average of 3.5 yards per carry. And Washington has been turning heads with the coaching staff, according to a post on the Raiders' YouTube page via Athlon Sports. But he needs to be better at pass protection . "He's a rookie, so he had a lot to catch up on," Kubiak said when asked about Washington's role in the passing game. "He's continuing to improve. (And) he's putting the work in. You see the practice come to life in the games. He's not where he wants to be. He's got to keep growing." Jeanty has been a threat in the passing game. Maybe his future is as a third-down back. Washington could supplant him. And the prediction is for that to begin this week. Jeanty has time to bounce back. It's still early in his career. But he simply hasn't been able to show in the NFL what he showed in college. away.blurb: The Los Angeles Rams are preparing to play the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 7, and the injuries just keep piling up. Earlier this week , the Rams placed wide receiver Davante Adams and nose tackle Poona Ford on injured reserve. Additionally, defensive lineman Kobie Turner has been ruled out for a handful of weeks. “Trent will be a DNP with his groin. We'll take it a day at a time, like what I told you guys, and evaluate his status as we go,” said head coach Sean McVay. “Then on Monday, found out Landman landed in the concussion protocol so he'll be a DNP.” While Landman's presence on the injury report isn’t surprising given that he’s been there the last few weeks, his placement in the concussion protocol is certainly a new development. In order to return to play, Landman will be limited in his allowed activity. He’ll then graduate to an aerobic exercise program overseen by the club’s medical staff. Lastly, after leaving Kobie Turner off the injured reserve transactions on Tuesday alongside Davante Adams and Poona Ford, the Rams placed him on injured reserve Wednesday. Turner will be out for a minimum of four weeks. In corresponding moves, the Rams signed EDGE Darryl Peterson III to the active roster and signed Jalen Hunt to the practice squad. “Everybody sees these and they're on their fantasy team or whatever and they're like, 'I have to trade a guy in and out now.' We're like, 'Well, that guy has worked his ass off for the last eight months to get this opportunity and it's unfortunate he doesn't get to do what he loves to do,’” said quarterback Matthew Stafford. “I feel more for our guys than I do for anybody else.I know the work that they put into it to be out here doing what they love, so that hurts me for them. But at the same time, I think I just feel even more responsibility to try to be as good as I can be to help us continue to win.” For the Raiders, defensive lineman Tonka Hemingway was the only non-participant as he remains in the concussion protocol. The Rams will certainly monitor the statuses of tight end Brock Bowers, offensive tackle Kolton Miller, and linebacker Quay Walker. All three were limited on Wednesday. However, the Rams will be monitoring other key starters as well this week. On Wednesday, cornerback Trent McDuffie didn’t practice with a groin injury and remains day-to-day. Additionally, linebacker Nate Landman has been placed in the concussion protocol. McDuffie was a late addition to the injury report last week. While McVay said that he felt good about him going into Sunday, McDuffie was inactive for the game. McDuffie will certainly be one to monitor this week. away.headline: Rams' rampant injuries are not a free meal ticket for the Raiders in Week 7
away.blurb: All-world defensive end Myles Garrett has been on the shelf for weeks and will not return to face Las Vegas in Week 7. But that is just the tip of the iceberg for the surprisingly 2-4 Rams. They'll also be without Davante Adams, Kobie Turner, Poona Ford, and potentially Trent McDuffie and Nate Landman. Landman is the Rams' starting WILL linebacker, and he makes a lot of good plays against the run and in space. It remains to be seen if he or McDuffie will play, but them starting the week as a DNP is not necessarily a good sign, and they could be playing at less than 100% if they do suit up. Raiders should remember Patriots beatdown and not count out injured foes Remember how confident fans were going into Week 5's game against the New England Patriots because they were down their top four cornerbacks and several other key players were limited or non-participants during the week? Rhamondre Stevenson, Christian Barmore, Christian Elliss, etc. If the Las Vegas Raiders want to right the ship in Week 7 and put an end to their three-game skid, it starts with addressing their own issues. Self-scouting is so important in the NFL. But the Los Angeles Rams are also coming into town this Sunday, and they are never an easy group to topple. Led by Sean McVay, one of the most brilliant minds in the sport, and with a star-studded roster that is apprepo for the city that they call home, the Rams pose significant challenges for a young Raiders team and coaching staff. As luck would have it for Las Vegas, though, LA is majorly banged up. They're not just dealing with depth injuries, either; several of their game-changers and biggest contributors will be on the sideline when the two teams take the field at Allegiant Stadium. That may sound like a free meal ticket and a huge advantage for the Silver and Black, and it is, in some ways. But the Raiders just learned in Week 5 that facing a short-staffed roster does not automatically lead to a win. In fact, it was a big, embarrassing lesson that they can't forget and surely haven't still less than two weeks removed from it. Key Rams injuries have piled up recently, and this week is the worst yet Adams went down with a ruptured hamstring in last week's loss to the Arizona Cardinals, and both Turner and Ford got hurt as well. Los Angeles isn't particularly deep at wide receiver, so it'll basically be Puka Nacua and some players that the Raiders wouldn't otherwise circle on the scouting report. Given Las Vegas' issues on the interior offensive line in recent weeks, the Rams not having Turner is massive. He's been a dual-threat this year, stopping the run and getting after the quarterback, so with Turner not playing, the Silver and Black have a lot less to worry about. This becomes especially true when one factors in the absence of Ford, who is a big nose tackle capable of plugging several holes by himself. Ford doesn't play many pass-rush snaps, but he is adequate in that realm as well. No Ford and no Turner is a godsend fo

Ilhan Omar says she will move out of her Washington, DC, home after federal search Today's E-Editions Chicago Tribune Advertise with Us Advertise with Us Branded Content Paid Partner Content Print (Opens in new window) Print Email a link to a friend (Opens in new window) Email 📮 Editorial Board endorsements ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. — The NFL on Monday suspended Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson for one game without pay for spitting in the direction of Las Vegas Raiders players on the field during a game a day earlier. Gardner-Johnson was ejected late in the second quarter for unsportsmanlike conduct following an exchange with a group of Raiders players, including tight end Brock Bowers. In issuing the suspension, the league cited its rule applying to “any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship.” With Buffalo (5-1) entering its bye week, Gardner-Johnson’s suspension will begin on Oct. 26 and run through Nov. 2, a day after the Bills host the Baltimore Ravens. The player has the right to appeal the suspension. Gardner-Johnson apologized to his teammates immediately following Buffalo’s 33-30 win, and has since posted a note on social media apologizing to fans. “I owe my teammates an apology and to be a man about it,” Gardner-Johnson said following the game. “You got to understand that as a grown man you can’t be doing (stuff) like that in a game,” he added. “As a vet, I’ll be better. I’ll take my consequences as it is, handle it like a man and move on.” The 28-year-old won a Super Bowl with the 2024 Philadelphia Eagles and is on his sixth team in eight seasons. Gardner-Johnson was signed by the Chicago Bears in October 2025 and appeared in 10 games with 51 total tackles. He signed a one-year contract with Buffalo in March. Coach Joe Brady referred to Gardner-Johnson’s spitting act as being “inexcusable,” and said he’s discussed the matter privately with the player. “It can’t happen. That’s not what we’re about. That’s not what the game of football is about, and he knows that,” Brady said. Gardner-Johnson arrived in Buffalo with an established reputation of being a noted trash-talker and as someone who has on occasion crossed the line with illegal hits. “I don’t need a roster of everybody being the same person,” Brady said. “Obviously, he crossed the line yesterday and that can’t happen. It won’t happen again. Personality-wise, I’m not afraid to have people who are going to try to toe the line in everything they do.” Also, the Bills are bringing back a familiar face with cornerback Tre’Davious White agreeing to sign to the team’s practice squad, a person with knowledge of discussions told The Associated Press. home.blurb: Rams Injury Report, Week 7 at Raiders: Puka Nacua and Trent McDuffie questionable, Nate Landman ruled out Skip to main content Primary nav TEAM WOODLAND HILLS, Calif. – Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua (calf) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Raiders at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas (1:25 p.m. PT, FOX). Nacua left Thursday's practice early with the aforementioned calf injury. Head coach Sean McVay on Friday said Nacua "took part in a majority of the practice, left, (and then) got it checked out." McVay also said that "I don't think he (Nacua) knows exactly when it occurred." Cornerback Trent McDuffie (groin) is also listed as questionable. McDuffie did not practice all week. Meanwhile, inside linebacker Nate Landman (concussion) was ruled out, but is "making good progress," McVay said. With Landman out, McVay confirmed Los Angeles will elevate inside linebacker Eric Kendricks from the practice squad. Both of these teams have playoff expectations in 2026, but they’re in very different spots through six weeks of the season. Seattle is coming off a bad loss to Denver on Thursday Night Football in Week 6, as Sam Darnold threw multiple picks and the Seattle offense struggled to get anything going against an elite Denver defense. That dropped the Seahawks to 3-3, and they’re multiple games out of first place in the NFC West. Meanwhile, the Kansas City defense put on a clinic in Week 6, holding the Los Angeles Chargers to just six points to move to 5-0 in the 2026 season. There is a huge revenge game possibly on Sunday, as Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III returns to Seattle for the first time since he won Super Bowl MVP for the ‘Hawks. The Seahawks let the star back go in free agency, and he’s been a monster for the Chiefs this season, rushing for 665 yards and six scores in just five games. Even though the Chiefs have a better record, Seattle is favored at home in this marquee matchup. Let’s take a look at the opening odds and some things to watch for in primetime in Week 7. Chiefs vs. Seahawks Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Chiefs +2.5 (-115) Seahawks -2.5 (-105) Seahawks: -135 42.5 (Over -105/Under -115) The Seahawks opened as just 1.5-point favorites in Week 7 , but the line has already moved to Seattle -2.5. There is clearly some confidence in this Seattle defense with an extended rest at home against Kansas City. The Chiefs have not lost this season, but they are banged up at the receiver position with Rashee Rice missing Week 6 and Tyquan Thornton on injured reserve. Oddsmakers seem to think this is a spot where the Chiefs will lose their first game in 2026. Chiefs vs. Seahawks Betting Preview These are two of the best defenses in the league, which isn’t what you’d usually think about when referring to a Patrick Mahomes-led squad. The Chiefs traded away Trent McDuffie in the offseason, yet they’re third in the league in EPA/Play and success rate and fourth in EPA/Pass. That could be an issue for a Seattle team that is heavily reliant on Jaxon Smith-Njigba, especially since Sam Darnold has thrown seven interceptions already this season. Seattle (No. 2 in EPA/Play on defense) completely shut down Bo Nix and the Broncos in Week 6, but it wasn’t enough with this offense still struggling. Seattle is just 25th in EPA/Play and 20th in success rate on that side of the ball through six games. It makes sense that the defending champs are favored at home, but there is one stat that I can’t look past when it comes to Mahomes. He’s been a road underdog 12 times in his career, going 10-1-1 against the spread and 9-3 straight up. The Chiefs look like one of the best teams in the NFL, and I expect that to remain the case in Week 7. I don’t mind getting 2.5 points with them as an early lean for this primetime matchup. Seattle outplayed Denver in a challenging short-week trip to the thin air of Mile High, but three turnovers left the Seahawks with a 17-14 loss despite outgaining Denver by 186 yards. The Seahawks are rested and ready with the infamous 12 on their side on Sunday night, presenting a much stiffer test for the undefeated Kansas City Chiefs . Kansas City hasn't run into a defense as good as Seattle's. Outside of a Week 1 win over the Broncos, the Chiefs have bullied defensive units currently ranked 21st or worse in Defensive DVOA. Seattle sits No. 2 in that popular advanced metric , and its four-man front is the reason why I'm taking the home team to win outright. That's shaking up the TD markets for running backs Emanuel Wilson and George Holani . Holani scored his first touchdown last week and was the Seahawks' weapon of choice in the second half, leading Seattle's RBs with a 58% snap share . LeBron's biggest comeback NFL predictions: 4 game picks for pivotal Chiefs-Seahawks matchup John Tapia Fri, October 23, 2026 at 2:00 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Sunday Night Football brings the Kansas City Chiefs to Seattle for a Week 7 matchup, also unofficially known as the "Kenneth Walker III Bowl." If you're looking for player props and game-day value, check out the latest lines at FanDuel Sportsbook before kickoff. The Seattle Seahawks are coming off of two straight losses and are staring a sub .500 record straight in the eyes. The Chiefs meanwhile are undefeated and are currently elated with their recent running back signing (and Offensive Player of the Year candidate) Kenneth Walker III. Let's look at some game picks ahead of this matchup Sunday Night. Kenneth Walker III over 84.5 rushing yards (-114) I know Walker III is not a Seahawk anymore. However, considering his dominance this season, and the Seahawks lack of dominant running game, this is surely the game pick on the top of everyone's mind. Walker III is averaging 133 yards per game this season . Meanwhile the Seahawks defense has not allowed a 100 yard rusher in a franchise record, 35 games – not since October 27, 2024. One of these juggernauts will have to break in this matchup. The betting line being at 84.5 seems to be lower than many expected, or at least lower than I expected. Walker III is on a career heater right now. His ability to flip the field at any moment and break any run into a house call is very rare. Even if the Seahawks defense holds Walker III in check, it only takes one explosive run to get close to this 84.5 line. On top of this, Walker III already gets a large share of carries, and is now facing a revenge game. I would expect Walker III to get a ton of carries in this game, which means tons of opportunities to hit this line. All of this considered, it is tough to see Walker III not being able to hit at least 85 yards rushing. That doesn't mean that he will break 100 yards – the Seahawks could still very easily extend their streak to 36 games. However, this will be their hardest challenge yet. The pick: Kenneth Walker III over 84.5 rushing yards . Over 42.5 points (-112) The line for this game is 42.5, also a little lower. The Seahawks have scored at least 29 points four times this season. Their only two games where they scored less was in Week 1 with Drew Lock coming in with no first team reps, and in Week 6 with a short week Thursday Night Football game. Add to this, the fact that the Seahawks are playing the red hot Kenneth Walker III and the Chiefs. There is a good chance that the Seahawks offense will need to keep up with Kansas City and their elite running game. That will surely be easier to do with Anthony Bradford and Zach Charbonnet likely returning for this game. Expect a high scoring affair in the battle of former AFC West foes. The pick: Over 42.5 total points (-112) . Jaxon Smith-Njigba over 92.5 receiving yards (-114). Leading the NFL in receptions (49), receiving yards (717), and receiving touchdowns (7) , JSN is once again on a heater. JSN has only missed the receiving yards line once this season – week 4 against the Los Angeles Chargers where he put up only 76 yards (18.5 yards shy of the line). With the Seahawks run game struggling, and Sam Darnold looking less confident week in and week out, expect the safety blanket, JSN to have another big game this week against the Chiefs. Despite averaging 143.4 yards per game, the lines still remain fairly low. With it this low, the smartest move would be to bet the over. The pick: Jaxon Smith-Njigba over 92.5 receiving yards . Zach Charbonnet to score 2+ touchdowns (+750) The first three picks may not be too risky. However, this last pick is very risky. Trying to correctly guess who will score two or more touchdowns is a Hail Mary of sorts, but why not live on the edge? Charbonnet, who was just activated off of the PUP list , is expected to make his season debut against the Chiefs. This season, the Seahawks have struggled in short yardage situations. That is exactly where Charbonnet's return is huge. When on the field, Charbonnet tends to find the end zone. Last season, Charbonnet led the Seahawks with 12 touchdowns. The year prior, Charbonnet had 8 touchdowns . Although this will be his first game back since tearing his ACL in the 2025 playoffs, look to see Charbonnet get these opportunities once again. It isn't just the short yardage situations however. Charbonnet is also a strong pass catcher and gives the Seahawks an opportunity to score as a receiver as well. Despite only having one career receiving touchdown, Charbonnet still has 95 receptions for 693 yards in his young three year career. The other elephant in the room with Charbonnet's return is Kenneth Walker III's absence. Throughout his career Charbonnet has always split the backfield with Walker III. However, this season Charbonnet has an opportunity to prove he is the clear number one running back. With Jadarian Price still on injured reserve, and the other running backs on the roster proving lackluster, this week will be a perfect opportunity for Charbonnet to prove he can lead this backfield. The pick: Zach Charbonnet to score 2+ touchdowns .

away.headline: Chiefs’ Latest Injury Report Raises Concerns About Travis Kelce, Rashee Rice, and Four Others Before Seahawks Game
away.blurb: According to the Chiefs’ official X account, “Travis Kelce, Cooper McDonald, L’Jarius Sneed, and Brashard Smith were limited in practice today. Jaylon Moore and Rashee Rice did not practice.” The Week 7 injury report highlighted that right tackle Jaylon Moore and wide receiver Rashee Rice did not participate in Wednesday and Thursday’s practices, while tight end Travis Kelce, linebacker Cooper McDonald, and cornerback L’Jarius Sneed remained limited. Besides them, running back Brashard Smith, who is also dealing with a hamstring, was held to limited on Thursday’s practice. WR Rashee Rice , who sustained a hamstring injury in Week 4, still remains ‘Questionable’ to play this Sunday as lingering issues prevented him from joining practice sessions ahead of their Seahawks clash. Travis Kelce, who tweaked his right ankle in the first quarter of the Week 6 game, is also ‘Questionable’ to play. After Kelce managed to return to the game and score four receptions for 53 yards on October 18. Chiefs head coach Andy Reid relayed the news that Kelce was going to be okay, albeit with some soreness in his ankle. But at 37 years old, it is still unclear whether the veteran tight end would be cleared this week. Both offensive tackles Josh Simmons and Jaylon Moore remained absent from practice on Wednesday. Moore suffered a concussion during the second quarter of the Week 6 Chargers game and was ruled out for the remainder of the game. After the diagnosis was confirmed, the tackle entered the NFL’s five-step concussion protocol. Meanwhile, Simmons, who had been struggling with a herniated disk in his lower back since August, was put on Injured Reserve again on Thursday, delaying his return. On the bright side, the Chiefs could finally see linebacker Cooper McDonald returning from Injured Reserve. The LB, who sustained an injury in Week 1, has been given a designation to return. The front office also waived Cam Jones and moved linebacker Aiden Fisher to the practice squad. The Seattle Seahawks will be a tough opponent for the Chiefs to crack, especially if starters like Travis Kelce and Rashee Rice are ruled out. It will be an especially significant game for Kenneth Walker III as the running back returns to Seattle to face off against his former Super Bowl-winning teammates. Linebackers Connor O’Toole (hamstring), Chazz Surratt, and Drake Thomas (ankle) did not practice on Thursday. On the other hand, LB DeMarcus Lawrence (not injury related/resting player, knee), quarterback Drew Lock (right elbow), and LB Uchenna Nwosu (hip) were all limited participants on the day. away.headline: Kansas City Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker refuses to make his return to Seattle in Week 7 to face the Seahawks any bigger than it is
away.blurb: Kansas City Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker refuses to make his return to Seattle in Week 7 to face the Seahawks any bigger than it is Skip to content Chiefs coaches have fielded questions all week about the return, and they don't expect it to get in the way of the task at hand. Their description of Walker was simple: Level-headed. His comments throughout the week reflect just that. Walker says he's treating this like any other week. Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy never returned to face a former team as a reigning world champion. He did face his former team as a player, though. The San Diego Chargers drafted Bieniemy in the 1991 NFL Draft, and he eventually played for the Cincinnati Bengals. Bieniemy didn't see the Chargers until Week 2 of the 1996 season. He had only two touches in that game: one carry for a 7-yard loss and a 9-yard reception. Regardless of the stat line, the experience gave Bieniemy insight into the emotions Walker could be feeling on Sunday night. Walker's RBs coach, DeMarco Murray, has also been through the same thing as a player. He faced the Dallas Cowboys as a divisional rival twice with the Philadelphia Eagles in the 2015 NFL season. Walker insists he won't make this matchup bigger than what it is. “It was mainly me and EB talking about how he went to a former team and how he felt about stuff, and you know, just giving me pointers on stuff like that,” Walker said. “But you just can't make it bigger than what it is. You know, I'm not the only one on this team. Everybody's going out there to play a game. I don't feel like it should be just about me.” That's the mentality of a true team player, and that outlook is part of what has made Walker's integration into Kansas City so seamless. He simply gets it. away.headline: Kansas City Chiefs Sign New Wide Receiver on Friday
away.blurb: Rice will miss Sunday night’s game at the Seattle Seahawks, the second consecutive contest he has been ruled out. The Chiefs have not received any limited practice participation from him this week. Entertainment Entertainment Home ··· Boxing The Kansas City Chiefs signed wide receiver Andrew Armstrong to the active roster from the practice squad on Friday, filling one of two open spots as Rashee Rice continues to deal with hamstring and knee injuries. Armstrong’s elevation marks his second appearance on the 53-man roster this season after he was called up for last week’s game against the Los Angeles Chargers. Official team channels confirmed the transaction late Friday. “Chiefs have filled one of their two open roster spots with WR Andrew Armstrong signed from the practice squad,” Matt Derrick of Chiefs Digest wrote . “RB Nate Carter takes Armstrong’s slot on the practice squad. He was dropped for the addition of LB Aiden Fisher earlier this week, but now he’s back.” Carter returns to the practice squad after a brief removal earlier in the week to accommodate linebacker Aiden Fisher. The move restores depth behind the running backs while Armstrong steps into the receiver group. In his only regular-season action so far, Armstrong recorded one reception for 13 yards on two targets against the Chargers. That catch produced a first down in a 22-6 victory that improved the Chiefs to 5-0. He started that contest and played 42 of the team’s offensive snaps, roughly two-thirds of the total, along with nine snaps on special teams. Coaches have noted his run-blocking reliability and route-running consistency as reasons for the increased role. Armstrong went undrafted in 2025 after a productive college career. He signed initially with the Miami Dolphins, later spent a short stint on the Detroit Lions practice squad, and joined the Chiefs on a reserve/future deal in January. At Arkansas in 2024, he led the Southeastern Conference with 78 catches for 1,140 yards. Those totals ranked second in school history for a single season and earned him first-team All-SEC recognition. During the 2026 preseason, Armstrong caught seven passes for 85 yards across three games. The production included several first-down conversions and helped him nearly earn a spot on the initial 53-man roster at cutdowns. Rice has totaled 13 receptions for 190 yards and one touchdown in three games this season before the injury. He entered Week 7 averaging 14.6 yards per catch but has not practiced since suffering the hamstring issue in Week 4. The Chiefs enter the Seattle matchup with the NFL’s only undefeated record in the AFC. They have scored 140 points while allowing just 83 through five games, ranking among the league’s top defenses in points allowed. away.headline: ‘He Will Get a Hero’s Welcome in Seattle’ — NFL Analyst Explains Why Kenneth Walker III Might Avoid Boos Despite $43.05M Move to Chiefs
away.blurb: Walker shared Seattle’s backfield with Zach Charbonnet for much of his time with the Seahawks, but Charbonnet was ruled out Friday and will not face his former teammate on Sunday. However, Walker was used as a bell cow down the stretch in the postseason and showed signs of what he is capable of if he were handed the lion’s share of the work. Only time will tell how the fans react to his return. It figures to be a key storyline during Week 7, and with the game on an island on Sunday Night Football, there figures to be plenty of discussion about it leading up to game time. Kenneth Walker III returns to Seattle in Week 7 to face his former team for the first time since signing with the Kansas City Chiefs in free agency. The reigning Super Bowl MVP has been a force for Kansas City, while injuries and inconsistency have plagued the backfield that he vacated. It’s unclear how Seahawks fans will treat Walker in his first game back, but one NFL analyst believes he will be received back with open arms by the home fans. Mike Florio Believes Seahawks Fans Will Cheer Kenneth Walker When He Returns as an Opponent in Week 7 “I would assume that he will get a hero’s welcome in Seattle,” Mike Florio said of Kenneth Walker III. “A lot of times, when a guy leaves in free agency, (the fans) boo. There is no cause; he wanted to stay, folks.” He carried the ball 65 times for 313 yards and four touchdowns, while adding in nine receptions for 104 yards in three postseason games, en route to being named the Super Bowl MVP. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor After the dominant playoff run, Seattle let the talented running back walk in free agency, instead opting to allocate their money to extend Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Devon Witherspoon, Derick Hall, and Rashid Shaheed. Walker then signed a massive three-year, $43.05 million contract with the Chiefs in free agency, with $28.7 million guaranteed. Through five games with the Chiefs, Walker has been worth every penny, ranking as the No. 1 running back in PFN’s Running Back Impact Metric , registering 106 carries for 665 yards and six touchdowns, while adding 14 receptions for 95 yards and two touchdowns. “It’s hard because he’s still wearing the wrong uniform on Sunday night, but they have their first opportunity to truly appreciate him since the day of the parade,” Florio added. However, those cheers may quickly dissipate if Walker rips off a few big runs or scores on the home team. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

home.blurb: Kansas City Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker refuses to make his return to Seattle in Week 7 to face the Seahawks any bigger than it is Skip to content Chiefs coaches have fielded questions all week about the return, and they don't expect it to get in the way of the task at hand. Their description of Walker was simple: Level-headed. His comments throughout the week reflect just that. Walker says he's treating this like any other week. Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy never returned to face a former team as a reigning world champion. He did face his former team as a player, though. The San Diego Chargers drafted Bieniemy in the 1991 NFL Draft, and he eventually played for the Cincinnati Bengals. Bieniemy didn't see the Chargers until Week 2 of the 1996 season. He had only two touches in that game: one carry for a 7-yard loss and a 9-yard reception. Regardless of the stat line, the experience gave Bieniemy insight into the emotions Walker could be feeling on Sunday night. Walker's RBs coach, DeMarco Murray, has also been through the same thing as a player. He faced the Dallas Cowboys as a divisional rival twice with the Philadelphia Eagles in the 2015 NFL season. Walker insists he won't make this matchup bigger than what it is. “It was mainly me and EB talking about how he went to a former team and how he felt about stuff, and you know, just giving me pointers on stuff like that,” Walker said. “But you just can't make it bigger than what it is. You know, I'm not the only one on this team. Everybody's going out there to play a game. I don't feel like it should be just about me.” That's the mentality of a true team player, and that outlook is part of what has made Walker's integration into Kansas City so seamless. He simply gets it. home.headline: Week 7 Injury Report: Chiefs at Seahawks
home.blurb: The Seahawks will be without running back Zach Charbonnet for another game. Charbonnet, who is working his way back from the torn ACL he suffered in the Divisional Round of the playoffs, practiced fully this week, but has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Chiefs. Also ruled out for the Seahawks are linebacker Drake Thomas , who will be out for the second week in a row due to an ankle injury, and linebacker Chazz Surratt , who will be missing a fourth straight game with a calf injury. Among those listed as questionable for the Seahawks is safety Nick Emmanwori , who was a new addition to the injury report on Friday, listed as limited due to a hip. Also questionable are outside linebackers DeMarcus Lawrence (knee) and Uchenna Nwosu (hip), both of whom were limited for the second straight day, backup quarterback Drew Lock , who has been limited all week with a right elbow injury, and outside linebacker Connor O'Toole (hamstring), who was limited Friday after not practicing the previous two days. For the Chiefs, starting right tackle Jaylon Moore is out due to a concussion. Left tackle Josh Simmons, who already missed the first five games of the season with a back injury, was placed on injured reserve earlier this week. Also out for Kansas City are receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) and running back Brashard Smith (hamstring). For the Chiefs, cornerback L'Jarius Sneed (knee) and linebacker Cooper Macdonald (knee) are both listed as questionable after being limited in Friday's practice. The Houston Texans are officially back, as is Caleb Williams with the Chicago Bears , and we have some serious questions about the Los Angeles Rams , who were upset by the Arizona Cardinals at home last Sunday. The Cardinals now have more wins at SoFi Stadium this year than the Rams and Los Angeles Chargers combined. This week, the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints will play the first-ever NFL game in Paris, the San Francisco 49ers look to remain perfect against the Atlanta Falcons , and Kenneth Walker III aims to lead the Kansas City Chiefs to victory over his former team, the Seattle Seahawks . This could be a revenge game for the ages. Which teams should you pick in Week 7, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 21 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. New England Patriots at Chicago Bears (-3) (TNF) Dajani (Bears -3): I can't remember the last time I've been this excited for a Thursday night game. Caleb Williams will suit up for the first time at home since his hamstring injury, and this is the first Bears home game since the passing of Mike Ditka. I have concerns about this Bears pass defense and how it will fare against a red-hot Drake Maye , but the fact is that Chicago has allowed 9.3 points per game at home this season. The Bears' offense has also averaged 35 points per game in their four wins, and I think Williams is out to make a statement. This will be a high-flying affair that comes down to the very end, and a push is very much in play. But give me Chicago at home, with the backing of an emotionally charged atmosphere. Remember, the Bears' lone Super Bowl win came against the New England Patriots under Ditka. … Prediction: Bears 28, Patriots 24 Dubin (Bears -3): I also see this being a high-scoring game, with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. … Prediction: Bears 31, Patriots 27 Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) vs. New Orleans Saints (Paris) Dajani (Saints +3.5): The Steelers are impossible to figure out. From week-to-week — or even half-to-half, as evidenced by last week's overtime victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . If you're going to give me the hook at +3.5 in an international game, I'm probably going to take it. The Saints are a perfect 8-0 ATS in their last eight games away from home, and are 3-0 ATS all-time in international games. I think Gayle Benson's recent comments stirred up the locker room, and the Saints responded with a win in which they dropped 34 points — even if it came against the New York Giants . … Prediction: Steelers 23, Saints 20 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): The Saints finally played a game from ahead last week against the Giants, and they didn't necessarily look comfortable doing it. They have mostly been a second-half offensive team throughout this season, struggling early on before piling up yards and points in comeback mode. I don't trust this offense enough to build a lead against Pittsburgh's defense (ninth in yards, 12th in points, fifth in EPA per play) right now, so I'll lean toward this game playing out in a similar fashion to New Orleans' early-season contests, with the Steelers taking a lead and the Saints trying to stage a comeback, only to fail this time around. … Prediction: Steelers 21, Saints 17 San Francisco 49ers (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): I'm thinking about backing the Falcons in this spot. The 49ers had an emotional victory over the Seahawks in Week 5 and are now on a short week after Monday night's win against the Washington Commanders . It looked like we were in for a blowout after the 49ers went up 23-3, but Washington then outscored San Francisco, 14-0, while outgaining the 49ers 201 yards to 7 yards. That was ... interesting to see. The 49ers have found a way to keep winning games despite all of the injuries. Nick Bosa , Mike Evans , Deebo Samuel , Upton Stout and Mykel Williams were among the players who did not practice on Wednesday. This week, I'm going to take the points with Atlanta. … Prediction: 49ers 22, Falcons 20 Dubin (49ers -3): This line feels several points too low, even with Mike Evans potentially out in addition to all of the other wide receiver issues. So long as the Niners have Kyle Shanahan calling plays and Brock Purdy , Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle involved, I think their offense cooks. And Atlanta can't quite reach the same level offensively — even with Bijan Robinson and Drake London on hand. The Niners have been excellent against the run this year, and if this game winds up being one where Penix has to match Purdy throw for throw, I don't see that going well for Atlanta. … Prediction: 49ers 26, Falcons 16 Cincinnati Bengals at Baltimore Ravens (-3) Dajani ( Bengals +3): The Bengals are fresh off their bye while the Baltimore Ravens are fresh off ... a loss to the Cleveland Browns . It was their 15th loss when leading by at least seven points in the fourth quarter since 2020, which ranks the most in the NFL. Lamar Jackson has a chance to return this week, but I'm curious to see how "spry" he looks. The two-time NFL MVP was playing some fantastic ball before the unfortunate ankle injury, and it's worth mentioning he's 7-2 in his career against Joe Burrow . I was high on the Bengals entering this season, and I'm not ready to move off that take. I think this Baltimore secondary is in for a tough test in stopping Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . The former averages 120.4 receiving yards per game vs. the Ravens, while the latter caught two touchdowns the last time he faced them. Higgins actually hasn't faced Baltimore since Oct. 6, 2024! It's been a while. Give me the upset here. We aren't 100% sure if Jackson is even returning to the lineup, and he'll have to face one of the best interior pass rushes in the NFL. Dexter Lawrence , Jonathan Allen and Kris Jenkins Jr. are the only defensive tackle trio to record multiple sacks this season. … Prediction: Bengals 29, Ravens 27 Dubin (Ravens -3): I'm assuming that Lamar Jackson is back for this game. If he's not, then you can switch my pick to the Bengals. If Jackson is in alongside Derrick Henry and Zay Flowers , I just don't think this Baltimore offense can be stopped. When those three have shared the field this season, the Ravens are averaging 9.9 yards per play. NINE POINT NINE. Unfortunately, the sample size is only 63 plays due to injuries to Jackson and Flowers at different times. HOWEVER, I will mention that Kelvin Sheppard 's unit forced five straight three-and-outs from the Cardinals in that 45-21 win in Week 5. Plus, Brian Branch is set to return to the lineup as well. "Your play-action pass game gets better and better as you run the football better," Head Coach Nick Sirianni said. "We know we have to play not only complementary football offensively, defensively, special teams, but also within the offense. Hurts missed this past Sunday's game after being diagnosed with a superficial blood clot. He had previously played in a loss to the Jaguars in London earlier this month. "Over the last few days, Jalen Hurts has received comprehensive medical evaluations by physician experts. In the interest of transparency, we are providing additional information on the diagnosis and treatment plan related to his condition. Jalen was initially diagnosed by specialists in London with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis. After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is a deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli. He is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations. His treatment should only involve anticoagulation (i.e. 'blood thinners'). During this time, he will not be allowed to participate in any contact activities, including football," the team announced. "Jalen's prognosis is very good, and we expect a full recovery. We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners. In the meantime, he will remain active around the team and continue to condition. More importantly, we anticipate that he will have no long-term effects. We are thinking of Jalen and looking forward to a strong recovery." Hurts last played in a loss to the Jaguars in London. He threw for 220 yards and one touchdown in a 19-17 loss.
